Overall: Simply the best contemporary action tower defense game. Worth a try for virtually everybody!
Summary; OMDU is the third installment in of the Orcs Must Die universe (following OMD1/2). It maintains much of what was fun about the predecessors while expanding on the formula in various ways. Most notably it has a party-style PVP-through-PVE mode called "Sabotage" where you play a PVE game where another party messes with you through more enemies and disruptive effects. Overall it's a new and improved OMD2, which I thought was one of the best coop games of its time.
Coop: OMDU allows for solo play and up to 3 player coop and 2v2 and 3v3 player PVE through PVP.
Performance: In-game the performance is very smooth. The action is fast and reactive. At high settings in extreme conditions the system can be bogged down, but this is very rare. The dashboard has some performance issues on my system, though I'm still figuring out the cause. Other games too can be slow such as exiting WoW, so it may be something with my system rather than the game.
Graphics: I love the cartoonish graphic style. Much improved from OMD2 largely indoor tunndels have been diversified into prisons, outdoor lush scenes, outdoor castle and harbour areas with arriving boats, various faction fortresses with indoor and outdoor sections and more. Hero animations are smooth and fun.
Sound: As with the original game, the music reinforces the fun quircky character of the game. The voice-over is marks the games light-hearted character and is of very high quality throughout (some large studios could take a lesson or two from it!). Sounds help guide what happens on the map not unlike previous games. The character quibs and banter is some of the best of any game I know.
Gameplay: The gameplay is close to OMD2 though drastically diversified by expanding the hero cast from 2 to over 10. Heroes offer a very diverse set of play styles from melee bruisers and tanks, to casters, to assassins, to support healers. Many abilities are visceral and fun (such as Bionka's bounce!). The game is still about a strong blend of hero ability use and trap damage, making it a strong hybrid of tower defense and third person action shooter. There is both a puzzle component to how to trap and build long paths, and an action component to execute. Failure is often hilarious and learning to improve is usually quite transparent from a failed attempt. Map variety keeps things fresh. There are many more enemies in OMDU than the previous titles and they bring not only more gameplay variety and puzzle aspect but also humor and charm. A big bear comes and tries to bounce you off the map, or a little runner spawns disruptive crystals all over the map while taunting you and evading your chases. Endless mode as in OMD2 still exists. Overall gameplay is close to the original formular but much expanded and improved.
Social: OMDU has guild and social chat support. One can play games with friends or find some though chat or matchmaker. The community is overwhelmingly friendly and supportive and the range of players include those who want to play a brief game of orc smashing to people who try to highscore endless or achieve high and crazy combos with their traps. Some will spend all their time in sabotage and enjoy the more competitive aspects. The game is well supported through forums, and a community run open discord.
Monetization/Value: The game uses a F2P model. This is a departure from the previous games which were for pay and had for pay expansions. I am not a huge fan of the model, but given what it is I think it is generally fair and at best extremely mildly P2W. Everything can be acquired through gameplay and the acquisition rate of chests and skulls (the main upgrade currency) is very sensible. One can use skulls to get all heroes and each hero can get a new chest on each map which in turn contain guaranteed skulls. My own stance was to look for ways to support the developers and I did this by buying all heroes and many skins. I have paid about a full price AAA titles worth so far. And if the game keeps adding content (which would fit a F2P model) I do plan to seek ways to support the title. However it is clear that none of this is required. Trap acquisition rate is a tad too slow for my taste and I wish devs would accelerate this a bit. Overall I think the F2P model is fair. I would only advice against buying trap chests. They are largely not worth your coin. Buy heroes instead and play the game to get chests there are literally hundreds of chests to acquire from gameplay alone.
Steam review score: At the time of this review the steam review score sits at 65%. I'll admit that my view of new games is swayed by these scores. I tend to hardly even look at games below 80% and usually start looking at 90%+. For me this is easily a 90%+ game and it is nowhere near a 65%. But of course games are in the eye of the beholder. This is not a game for anybody who hates action tower defense games. Nor is it a game for anybody who absolutely want to pay a full box price before trying a game because "all F2P games are P2W". It is however an amazing game that I can recommend to almost anybody for some exceptional fun and humor and the best way to currently scratch any action tower defense gameplay itch!
My background: I was a big fan of OMD2 which, when it came out was my favorite coop game. When I got a chance to join the closed beta for OMDU I did even though then it had a strong MOBA/PVP only focus. The game has since changed drastically and basically has become what I was hoping to get, which is new an improved OMD goodness! I have hundreds of hours in the game and am not tired of it yet! I sure do hope that Robot keeps doing what they have been doing, which is adding every new goodness to the OMDU playform. But even if not I got tremendous value from the game already!

So when I heard Paul was back making GalCiv3 I had to go check it out. Then I find out could preorder the Elite Founders Package and get all future content for $99. It took me all of about 3 seconds to log in and buy Gal Civ3. I have been playing a few games a week since. I will admit I played more GalCiv2 than GalCiv3 in Alpha, but I have not even played GalCiv2 in about 2 months.
GalCiv3 is shaping up to be the best space 4X game that has ever been made. The game is about to be released and most all the major CTD or game stopping bugs have been fixed. Now I find myself playing a game as often as I can with several over the weekends.
Here is what I love about the game: (I have about 350 hrs of game play atm)
-Graphics- Brilliant!!!
-Maps-
Huge maps up to 5 times the size of GalCiv2, but I mainly play on Huge.
-Anomalies-
I love getting anomalies with my flagship. I really like atm you can buy the other races flagships to hunt even more anomalies. I am sure this will get fixed soon thou. Also I hope they add back the color system of the anomalies from GalCiv2. I hate clicking on a wormhole until all the good anomalies are gone from my area.
-Pirates-
It will be nice when Stardock upgrades them to be more like Sins. I would love to pay or give ships to the pirates to attack random AI players. Paul said there is more planned options but for a latter DLC.
-Adjacency system-
Basically you have to place like buildings near each other to boost the value. Also with this new system there are lots of building types and not all races have the same buildings.
-Terraforming-
There are lots of terraforming options. Now when you look at the planet management screen you see a map with land masses. Pretty much every hex you see that is on land you will eventually be able to terraform it. Oh how I miss the galactic wonder to auto update all tiles from GalCiv2.
-Tech Trees-
Each race has its own tech tree. Each tree has 4 areas (Colonization, Engineering, Warfare, and Governance) that are spaced out over 3 ages. A player has to think about what to upgrade now vs just getting to the best weapon/def combo and kill everything.
-Starbases-
I love building these. I swear I build a neutral zone with one of these every few inches on my boarders. The same bases are back and we get a new one, Mining. Now there are tradable resources to mine for new buildings, weapons, and ship support systems. I will admit I cannot wait until there is an auto build click option for upgrading Starbases. I swear I spent most my time sending constructors to Starbases. At least this time you can have more than one module on a constructor.
-Shipyards-
This go around not every planet can make a ship. At first I hated this. Now with having a shipyard being sponsored with up to 5 planets you can manage you ship building much more easily. Plus with a great planet set up you can build huge ships in just a few turns.
-Battle viewer-
Watching your ships in action is great the first few times in a game. Then after you have 20+ battles a turn you are happy Stardock left in the old auto resolve option. I hope they add a click option to always auto resolve. I will turn in on after I have 5+ fleets in action.
-Shipbuilding-
This time around the default ships are not that bad…Still mine are way better…
-Fleets-
This time around you cannot just spam build one type of ship. You need assault ships, escorts for your larger ships, guardian ships for your carriers. YES we have carriers this time and they are currently very OP. They start each battle with a number of drone ships loaded up with your best tech to kill all aliens in your path.
-Custom races-
This just got put in and I love it. I am making races left and right. The default ones are pretty easy to beat. I need more options: logos, pictures, backgrounds, etc… I keep hearing Paul talk about Jennifer, I think that is her name, and how she is god’s gift to coding most of all the goodies in the game along with the UI.
-Ideological Traits-
Basically your good, evil, neutral options. This time your actions take one of 3 paths which give points to buy traits in one of the three trees. You can stay in one tree or spread them out over all of them. Down side is the more you buy the more it costs. So maxing out all the trees is pretty impossible now. I only can pick about 20% of 1 tree now. The points are still under progress I am sure they will change upward soon.
Things I know will get fixed and I am holding my breath waiting
-AI-
One of the things I loved about GalCiv2 was the AI. GalCiv2 has 12 levels of difficulty and I have only been able to win on level 9 and that is only about 25% of the time. I think one of my best memories of the AI in GalCiv2 was when I was building up my fleets near the neutral zone getting ready to invade when the AI contacts me. I get a message that he has seen me do this before and he attacks me before I am ready and the game was over. Currently I am unable to lose on GalCiv3 the AI just is unable to anticipate my game play or put up much of a challenge. This is not to say it will be that way for everyone. I do have a million or more game plays since 2003. Brad will fix this. He likes it when the AI beats up on players…..
-Diplomacy-
I love the current UI, the concept, and all the options. The only problem is the AI does not value things the way a player does..YET! Devs read the forums every day and update the AI based on player’s feedback. Although it is pretty fun to sell things I never need to the AI for items they need but think they are better suited in my hands….ha-ha
-Control N-
I think I miss this option more than any other option from GalCiv2. If you do not know that is how you can restart a game once you have loaded up a map if you do not like what you see. Also works anytime in the game.
-Ship Builder-
Better UI management and easy way to sort ships you want to use. In GalCiv2 it was easy to only have a few ships at a time in your window to choose from, here not so much.
-Steam workshop support-
I cannot wait to see what the players come up for mods to play with this game. I also hate building ships but love downloading great ship builder’s designs to use in my games….

En Este Review dare mi Opinion de Hotline Miami con sus Pros y Contras
--------LORE--------
Controlamos a Jacket, un Hombre Normal el Cual tiene su departamento, Un Día Comienza a tener Llamadas estrañas las cuales lo mandan a Hacer Algunos Recados, los Cuales son Matar Mafiosos Rusos y Maleantes, Para empezar nos Dan una Simple mascara para ir a Completar nuestros Recados, Segun la historia, Si no se Cumplen las ordenes podrán pasar cosas malas en tu entorno. Así que Obligatoriamente Nos Tendremos en Nuestro DELOREAN a Nuestras misiones.
En uno de sus Trabajos, Jacket encuentra a una Chica la cual estaba Secuestrada, el Protagonista la lleva a su departamento y empiezan a convivir (Mientras hace todos esos Brutales Recados). Durante el Juego, iras encontrando mascaras que te daran habilidades.
--------PROS--------
-. A Pesar de ser Un Juego totalmente hecho con Pixeles, Le da su toque de los 80', Lo Cual te hace sentir verdaderamente bien con el juego.
-. La Dificultad va Variendo cada nivel que avanzas del juego
-. Al las mascaras tener habilidades, Esto te da muchos estilos de Juego los Cuales Probar.
-. a Pesar de que el juego no tenga Mucho Dialogo o "Cinematicas" te deja Bastante clara el desarrollo del Personaje y su Historia.
-. Es un Juego bastante Desquitante en el cual puedes descargar todo lo que tienes matando Mafiosos.
-. Los Combos te dan el Objetivo de pasar Los niveles cada vez Mejor para llegar a sacar una A, una A+ o una S.
-. Un Muy Buen soundtrack, la Musica es uno de los Factores mas importantes del juego, Le da su "Toque".
----CONTRAS----
-. La IA Es un Poco rara a veces y te acaba Matando de maneras un poco extrañas.
-. Algunas Mascaras son Totalmente inservibles y Algunas a veces demasiado Rotas.
-. Muchas veces Alguien Nuevo en el juego no sabe que tiene que hacer en algunas Misiones espicificas.
-. No se Puede saltar Directamente las escenas del Departamento de Jacket despues de pasar de un capitulo a otro.
-. El juego a veces Crashea sin saber por qué, perdiendo todo tu progreso si hacias un SpeedRun o colectabas las Letras Secretas.
------RECOMENDACIONES-------
-. No Juegues con Ningun Tipo de mando, solo se te hara mas dificil jugar, el Teclado es lo mejor para jugar este juego.
-. No Te tires a lo Loco contra los mafiosos.
-. No desactives la Música, es lo Suficientemente buena Como para disfrutarla mientras Lo Juegas.
-. Intenta Comprender la Historia del Personaje.
-. Prueba Todas las armas y Mascaras que puedas para variar el juego y hacerlo mas divertido.
-------Conclusion---------
Hotline miami es un Buen juego para pasar el rato y desquitarte, te asegurara mucha diversion las horas que dura, Lo encuentro en muchos casos mejor que el Hotline Miami 2, No Dudes en Comrarlo si lo ves en oferta.

Back in the day, I've loved Mafia II. That's the reason why I've trusted and pre-ordered this game. Even I've know the fact we play someone else in III (like we play Vito in II instead of Tommy), maybe game reveal what the actual ♥♥♥♥ happened after the events of II.
Well, the day come and I've pre-load hella gigabytes, it turns out this game ported on PC ♥♥♥♥♥♥! Like tons of other games! I leave this game to dust after 10 hours of strugge low performance and lots of bugs.
After I've take a brand-new GPU and hear this game gets some little bit performance fix patches, I decided to give this game another shot. Here's my thoughts about Mafia III.
We are playing as a war veteran named Lincoln Clay. Clay doesn't have too much enemies when he got back in town. Town's godfather Marcano offered a job to Clay, but he immidetly refuses it, because he didn't want to take job from who adopted him. Marcano betray to Sammy and takeover everything that he owns, and ended up killing all relatives he got. Somehow, bullet misses Clay, and he survived. And in that point, this game's story is taking back what's yours. It's revenge time for us.
While this game kinda weak on telling on story, because it's arcade-gameplay nature, Story is hella cool. Also game reminds we are a colored-person everytime, like everyone reminds them in 60s. Game really has a good atmosphere, and if you are a story person, you'll probably like it.
Gameplay elements are far away from both Mafia I and Mafia II. This game has an arcade nature and stealth elements unlike other games in the series. Mafia was a real-life simulation back in the day, and there was only few stealth sections. Well maybe other hardcore fans doesn't like this, but I did. I love this kind of gameplay and if I've a choice to chance between them, I would probably choice Mafia III's gameplay even it missed lots of things. Yes it missing things, but I will not going to mention this. I don't want to make this review a comperasion between other games.
You have insticts which show enemies behind walls and that've been popular after 2012, every game adds this feature while they haven't make something like this before. I could give Hitman and Tomb Raider as an example. Mafia added this feature to itself too and it helps a lot. But is it necessary? I don't think so.
Close combat is awesome! You can charge and attack someone, make a lethal grab, or blast their face with your shotgun. Mafia II and I has fighing mechanics which is kinda of hard and cool, but this game makes it easy and fun! It makes you feel stronger then every other guy you about to hunt.
Car mechanics gone lot easier. At day one, there wasn't a thing called slow-motion, but they have added this as a feature later, which is I don't have anything to say about it. It comes handy and makes driving lots of easier. Only thing I mention about driving is I missed to obey traffic rules, this game not forces you to make it.
Like other Mafias, this is a open-world game too, but unlike them this game isn't force you to play game by chapters. You have freedom to make everything. But it feels not so filled, you have few things to collect, few sidemissions to make and few races and other kinds of stuff to complete. Well other freeroam games can't make a loaded map too, I don't count this one as a cons.
Even I've sounded like this game is awesome, it's clearly not. It has lots of bugs, bad performance and rushed elements. This is 2K's fault they have forced devs to rush this out. However, this game is still enjoyable. I hardly recommend this, even on sales, but if you are conviced yourself to buy this and want to check out reviews, you can try it. If you have mediocre PC build, you can play this on 50-60FPS with 1080p resolution.
So, I hate when I can't objectify something as YES or NO. This is directly between them. If you think your PC powerful enough, you can try this, give a shot, It's a cool game.

Aight, this game gets a lot of hate, some of it warranted, but I actually enjoy it, here's my good and bad list, starting with the cons:
- Optimization is really half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the only game that runs this bad on my rig is Dishonored 2 and Arkham Knight, both similar clusterf*cks
- Graphics are simultaneously gorgeous and 2010-level, depending on where you are in the city and what time of day it is. It's generally blurry and colorless (no racist pun intended LULZ), so IMPORTANT TIP: start by installing the Reshade/SweetFX mod which improves a TON on the visuals, it's how the game should've been released, and makes sooo much difference.
- No fast travel, which I understand is more immersive, but objective placement especially with the side missions leads to quite a bit of tedious driving with the era-specific slow cars.
- Bushes behave like concrete blocks, drives me mad
HOWEVER:
- '60s atmosphere is spot-on
- cutscenes and voice acting are probably some of the best you will see and hear in a videogame
- Most importantly, the moment to moment gameplay is very entertaining, whether it's the action-movie style car handling, the BRUTAL executions, satisfying shooting and cover mechanics, or sneaking around headshotting goons with silenced weapons.
It's the latter point which draws me back to the game often, despite having finished it already. The chunky physicality of the entire game has a feel to it that I always start to miss after a while, and it makes me reinstall the game. The slightly repetitive structure of the game might make it boring if you were to mainline the game, but in short bursts it's really fun to play.

Lots of seafaring fun with all of it's parts.  Like a lot of games it can be exasperating at times especially when your maxed out fleet loses to a wimpy faction.  Not a whole lot of differences no matter what level you play at except on Easy you don't have to worry that a port won't buy your cargo or that your homeport won't like any of their cargo.
There are 2 methods of combat.  You can control all your ships in a high resolution graphic war or use Autoresolve that determines the winner.   At first I used the graphic option but found that controling 5 warships was a problem, especially since more often than not your surrounded by islands that will rip ships apart and the ships are not capable of sharp turns.  The enemy of course is on the seaward side of the islands.  Additionally your ships will not fire near as often as the enemy.  If you put all the ships on auto except the flagship they will run right into an island and sink.
The skill your Captains receive for destroying enemy ships are pretty much useless.  They can still be womped by a wimpy enemy and they will sooner or later.
The Galleon is a bit over rated in the game.  It is a slow clumbersome ship more suited for cargo but the game lists it as a war ship.  Back in those days a Scooner captained by an experienced captain could defeat one.  The trick was to sail around behind them and hit them from behind.  Another trick was to watch for the flash of the Galleon's cannon.  Unlike shells of today it took a while for the cannon balls to reach you.  You knew that the Galleon would be leading his target so a quick turn to the port or starboard would cause a miss.  You didn't want to get hit by them even once!
When the Frigate came out most nations switched to it because it was faster and more manuverable that a Galleon.
Enuf of the history lesson, lol.  It's a fun game if you like strategy sea wars.

Dust: An Elysian Tail is one of a kind, a true gem shining in the sea of indie game developing. The story is wonderful, the art is fantastic, the dialogues little below perfect, and the gameplay is just a ton of fun.
Dust himself, to say it shortly, is a total badass. 20 monsters in the screen at once? Piece of cake. 30? Child's play. 40? Puh-leeze! And the creators mixed the exact amount of story and character into the storm of sword strikes. He's emotional, caring, funny and mysterious, with a great backstory to go with it. The Sen-Mithrarin concept is so creative I might just steal it sometime I'm writing.
Fidget steals the spotlight all the time. Either she's making you bust a gut laughing or clogging your eyes and nose from emotion, and she's so darn cute you want to squeeze her into putty. And Ahrah fulfills the role of guide and mentor perfectly.
The rest of the characters had understandably little space in a 16-hour game, but most of the time you are able to understand and relate to them. There were one or two I wish were given more screentime, especially Haley.
The gameplay is very well balanced, with exploratory platforming that'll make you scratch your head wondering where the hell that treasure is or how do you get to it, and ploughing through hordes of monsters is a fun experience you hardly ever get tired of. The only shortcoming of the gameplay aspect (hell, maybe the whole game) is the small combo library. You gain access to Dust's whole melee arsenal before finishing the first region. I would have liked to see more combinations and versatility, even though you never get tired of using those handful of combos you're given.
All in all, 4.999999999999999999999999999999999999 out of 5. A game so good for this price is something no one should miss.

TLDR: It's a good game. I recommend you download it.
Paladins delivers a fun, unique class-based shooter experience that I would definitely recommend.
Contrary to popular belief,
Overwatch Clone:
I do not feel like this is a "Overwatch Clone", while the style and several heroes feel like Overwatch characters, it plays much different.
It embraces more of the shooter aspect of "Class-Based Shooter" than Overwatch. In Overwatch, you have characters using a variety of ways to damage and kill enemies, while most Paladins characters use guns or things seen in other First-Person Shooters. The addition of mounts and other features not seen in Overwatch give it it's own personality.
Characters:
The characters are done very well. Each feels unique and fun, and has a clear-cut playstyle. No character feels the same (except Tyra and Viktor's abilities are pretty similiar, but I digress.) and no one hero is stronger than the other. Each has equal power.
New heroes are released fairly frequently, and that is a good
Abilities:
The abilities are also a strong point in the game, each character's abilities feel different to the other (except the aforementioned Viktor and Tyra.)
I do feel that some abilities should be changed. I feel Lex's Retribution should be changed, as the reward for killing the target is a measly few credits, and you usually will never be able to buy anything from the shop even if you kill all your targets. Using the ability is useless as well, because after your target is killed you get a random one anyway, so using it has no value.
I feel changing it so the reward feels more... rewarding could give much more incentive to play him. (I will add that using the card loadouts you can gain e.g. lifesteal for killing the target, but that isn't part of base Lex and the point still stands.)
Customization:
You can change things like your skin, emote and card loadout. While it adds a nice touch, it should definitely be fleshed out more, because right now there are very little options (but this will probably be changed when the full game is released.)
The card loadouts are done very well, they change the playstyle and gameplay of a character quite a bit. It is easy to get more cards by opening the packs or buying them with the currency (which you get a lot of.)
I hope HiRez expands the customization, because it is overall luke-warm.
Graphics/Art Style:
The art style is very pleasing, looking a lot like a Pixar film. The graphics are good, and even I can run it at a decent framerate and good graphical setting. I think HiRez did a good job on that.
Skill Cap:
It does feel more casual than most other competitive class-based shooters, but it does have the potential to be competitive. The competitive mode is out and, while I haven't played it yet, I think it could blossom into something great.
Gameplay:
The gameplay feels fair and balanced. Fast paced, almost non-stop action. Mounts work well to get you to the fight ASAP, and the abilities compliment the gunplay pretty well. If you find a cooperative team, which seems to happen more than most other games, you can have a fun game.
Overall:
It is a good game, with fun gameplay and graphics. Characters and abilities flow well and compliment gameplay greatly.
While there are some things that I think should be fixed/furthered, like some abilities and customization, the game is great. Would definitely recommend.

This game is exactly what it says it is, a mash between the roguelike genre and rhythm games. But it is more than that. The first guideline is fairness : It is one of the only fair roguelikes. When you die, you will be able to watch the replay of your last few moves so you can understand what killed you and why. I have played this game for almost 100 hours, and never have I felt like my death was unfair. It was always my own fault, so I couldn't blame the game for anything. And that takes the frustration out of the experience.
The second one is mastery : while you will have to learn a few patterns and item effects, they are pretty straightforward, and the game has a training room where you can learn at your own pace everything you want to learn. But the real difficulty comes in when you have to adapt to those patterns, dance with the enemies without making a mistake, and when there are multiple enemies, you'll have to keep track of what each of them is doing and adapt to the situation. This would be easy to do if it wasn't for the time restriction : you can't stay here and think, you have to keep moving to the beat. That is why you need mastery : the ability to master the patterns to a point where they become second nature, for you won't have time to think, only react.
Put these two wors together, and you get Crypt of the Necrodancer : difficult but fair.You won't need luck or knowledge, you won't need any wiki to remember what every item does, the only thing you'll need is yourself, your brain, your reflexes, your skill. Are you up to the task ? Can you manage to defeat the Necrodancer and escape from the Crypt ? You are the ony one able to answer that question.

I purchased Galactic Civilizations III through the Founder program--I loved Galactic Civilizations II  and was excited by the prospect of seeing the next chapter of the game develop.
Simply put, the game is fantastic.
The stunning art and amazing score create an immersive experience far above that of GalCiv2.
The planet management aspect of the game gives players a number of strategic choices as different planets have differing qualities (i.e., number of usable tiles), varying layouts, special characteristics (e.g., increased manufacturing), bonus-granting tiles, and special resources that can be traded. Some of this is similar to GalCiv2, but with the addition of adjacency bonuses, improvement choices and placement is far more strategic.
One of the major design differences between GalCiv2 and GalCiv3 is that shipyards are now in space and can receive sponsorship from multiple planets. This makes them strategically important as they become targets for your enemies, but it also enables you to choose whether to position shipyards with several sponsors (and a greater manufacturing capability, which is better for more expensive ships) or create a shipyard for each planet.
The tech tree for each race is unique and offers a huge number of strategic paths for players to follow. The improvements you build on planets, the components you add to ships, and much more depend on the techs you research, so the way you advance through the tech tree matters. And the variety of techs within each race's tree, as well as the even greater variety from race to race, means that all kinds of play styles are viable.
Probably my favorite aspect of the game, the ship designer is remarkably powerful and allows you to create custom ships in great detail. It's easy to spend hours designing hulls and equipping them with your latest functional components.
I could go on: the sheer size of the maps is mindblowing (e.g., on the largest size, insane, you'll be exploring for hundreds of turns); the max number of AI players is huge (100+); the ability to create your own factions (with and without modding) adds another level of personalization to the gameplay experience; and most important of all, the game is just fun.
And one thing I've learned while observing the development cycle: Stardock is an amazing company with a development team that listens to feedback and cares about its fans.
I couldn't be happier with the investment I made purchasing this game.

I am not speculating my doubt on how much I like this game when I state this, but I am questioning the logic of the depth of the basements. Maybe Mom planned for Isaac to escape her grasp, so that he may be tortured by the beasts underneath?...

I just want to have fun.

I'm happy to have bought this on discount. It's not a world apart from SCS' "Bus Driver Gold". If you enjoyed that, I think you will enjoy this too. In Bus Simulator 16's favor, it's a bit more detailed in its technical nature than the SCS game, but going against it - the world in Bus Simulator 16 is somewhat un-inspired. It's all flat, urban territory - the challenge of the actual driving is somewhat tame. But, dealing with customer change and minor issues that occur, both in the bus and in the urban world, are a nice touch. Steam achievements aren't flung at you so it's nice to come across them when you do, and the challenges (missions or tasks etc) determined from the menu map screen are pretty good.
It seems to run in the districts with heavy animations/objects at about half speed on my machine, as each second in-game lasts about 2 seconds. I'm not sure if that's the intention, but I must also point out that on loading I am told by the game that my system does not meet the minimum specs. So I'm just glad it works, even if it is in slow motion some of the time. I'm so used to running most games on their lowest settings, I can't really complain about the graphics. Slower gameplay would normally really annoy me but here I've found it tolerable. I'd like to try this game (and many others) on a better rig sometime... With all that said, it takes a little while to get used to the steering and learning the length of your bus, but it's not long before you can roll quickly, smoothly (and safely) around.
The only thing that has really struck me as "Aww, why isn't that there?" are the pictures of your buses on the Bus Inventory screen remaining as the stock images and not your customization. It's very minor...but, as you can name the busses, it'd be nice to see the appropriate bus that you've named so you can familiarize yourself with it. The stock images are pretty dull and, as you progress and earn money and have a whole fleet of customized busses - the images don't really reflect the situation well at all.
Overall it's a nice game to play having played SCS Bus Driver Gold in the past. It's a little bit bleaker compared, but what it lacks there it makes up for in some nice technical additions that Bus Driver Gold never had. As they never made a sequel, I guess in a way you could say Bus Simulator 16 is it. Aside from comparing those 2, if you compare the missions of this simulator to say the London Underground one, it's far superior. And yes, the voice acting in Bus Simulator 16 is a bit creepy, but doesn't really detract from it overall... It's a quirky game set in a quirky place. But it may be best to get it at a quirky price.

Originally released for the Xbox 360, Dust: An Elysian Tail is proof that ports can be done near-perfectly if you just pay enough attention and respect to the material. The port to the PC side of things is so impressive, it blows other studios out of the water, beating out large developers and publishers like Activision and in some cases even EA.
Dust: An Elysian Tail is beautiful in all its artwork. Visually unique, stunning, and well crafted. With unique characters all designed and drawn by one person, Dust AET really showed the focus and talent that Dean Dodrill has. While voicework, soundtrack and a few other aspects were done by contract, it was all pulled together by one person and that makes this even more impressive.
Combat is tight, quick, and avoids the pitfalls that cause most brawlers to fail in my eyes. I don't have to feel like I'm spamming buttons to do what I want to do, instead there's a weight to actions that give a clear cause-and-effect between button presses and combinations that provides for a better sense of play. The RPG aspects of the game allow for a level of customization which also is an added benefit to replayability.
The soundtrack, contracted through Hyperduck Soundworks is nothing short of impressive. While previous offerings by Hyperduck didn't particularly impress me (mostly in part due to the game they were designed for didn't catch my attention), Dust:AET's soundtrack is one that grabbed me from the title menu all the way through. Tracks compliment not only environment, but the overall "goal" for passing an area. Large sweeps of various instruments while keeping a higher tempo help build an urge to get through zones in open environments.  Heavier claustrophobic tracks help reinforce the underground nature of various caverns and all the tracks push you to want to see what is on the next screen.
You would be excused if you weren't sure Dust: AET was a native game for the PC. Extensive PC options for video, audio, and controls are something that even massive publishers fail to do are all present but it even has options to customize the size of the UI as well as position. The game plays well with keyboard and mouse (though admittedly I preferred to play with a controller, having the best of both worlds makes the PC an excellent platform), and it even scales extremely well for slower PCs and laptops.
This is a great platformer, and if you're looking for one that is technically competent, an excellent experience, and one that manages to strike that chord that most art pieces try so hard to do then Dust:AET is a game you simply must get and play. Whatever you do, make sure you have either excellent speakers, or headphones. Audio design is just that great.

Have no fear, this game is completly abstinent! But I think that's to be expected from a game rated E 10+!
Dust is an action, platforming, RPG. The sole mechanic is the "Dust Storm", a special move that lets you glide through the air and attack enemies. This move assists in combat as well as platforming.
The game's level design is split up so that you are platforming half the time, and the other half you are mowing down bad guys. It is unfortunate that there are only two distinct moments when you are doing both at the same time, and I would have appreciated more moments that combined combat and platforming.
Many areas are blocked off at the beginning of the game until you unlock the special ability that lets bypass the specific obstacle blocking your way. These blocked off areas don't conceal anything super special, but I find a lot of joy exploring the map trying to find all the hidden chests.
The story is well written and well executed, and kept me engaged the entire time. There were certain sad moments that didn't effect me that much, but the chills I got at the cutscene before the final boss made up for that! There were countless jokes thrown in along the way that made me laugh!
Overall, I think the game was a pleasent expierence and I would strongly recommend it!

I'm a 40 year old gamer who has played just about every great strategy game and an avid gamer of all game types. At this point I'm torn if I can recommend the game to everyone. As a big fan of GAL CIV 5 I gotta say I really do like the concept and the direction it goning. I know it's in Beta, BUT we could be getting close to final by now. So i'm a little worried it isn't going to be everything I dreamed it would be. After spending a few days in the game (26 hours) I must say there are some things that I wish were different. I played three different rounds. The one I got the furthest on was a medium galaxy with default settings. I love good strategy games and after about 15 colonies things started to drag for me at around turn 280... i was about 15 hours into this game. So here is my review:
What I liked:
- Creating your own race is good fun and well done... long live the F.U.Z.Z.I.E.S. My furry chipmunk race! ;-)
- Exploration and growing your empire is spot on! Love it.
- Using constructors to build starbases to expand your empre is a great concept. (cultural, military, mining, etc.)
-  Diplomacy seemed to work very well! I liked how the races would barter with you and give you an idea of if you were close in your negotiation. Great job to the devs on this idea!
- The mods you can build on the planet as you climb the research ladder is great. Also the way the interface is setup is very intuitive and works great.
- Great interface that easy to play and learn, but complex enough to give you the power you need to grow your empire effectively. It didn't take me long to figure out what i was doing and how it is done. The mouse-overs do a great job explaning the game.
What needs improving "in my opinion" to make this a 5 star ALL-TIME favorite game: (which i would hope the dev's will really hear my out on this!")
- Space battles suck... they are no fun at all. Period! THe options: either watch the fight play out with no control or direction to your ships, or just hit autoresolve. So every time I would fight i would just auto-resolve, because otherwise it was just a waste of time watch the ships shoot lasers at each other randomly. NO strategy or control here? Also the autoresolve battles take longer than expected... like it stalls.. makes some "pew pew" sounds to give you a conclusion. And the conclusion is either your ship disappears or your opponents does. There are no gooey details, no stats screen on what happened, and they basically fall completely flat. (I will say invading planets is much better at least there is a stat screen that pops up)  Even with this fact, the game can still be fun, but does drag due to this fact. If the battles were fun and something to look forward too i think the balance of this game would be perfect. At this point in it's current state it isn't going to win any awards and will get maybe a 74 to 82 metascore at best. Which isn't bad, but it could be sooooo much better!
- Allow some of the starbases to be self-upgrading. Having to send a constructor to the starbase everytime for an upgrade is too tedious and time consuming. Maybe for major things require a constructor, but not for every single upgrade please.
- Give more explanation on the options you can choose when creating your universe. There isn't enough on screen destription on all the options you can tweak. You could even show some screen shots of a tiny map, medium, large... with stats below it that say how many planets there will be, and what % will be habitable, etc. etc.
Lastly.... I can't stress enough on how much potential this game has if ONLY the space battles had personality and some sort of action/strategy. It would be awesome if you controled your ships with diablo style mouse clicks and hit keys for the different weapon options like 1 key would be lasers, 2 key would be missles, 3 key kinectic blast, 4 rail gun, etc. You get the idea. Make it work like you control your party in Pillars of Eternity ... they concept they have to control a party of six characters issuing orders to each of them would be brilliant in this game. Check it out devs! Do it and i guarantee you will have a 5 star 90+ meta rating score game and will please your fans. Balance in games is so important and this game has so much strategy and slow pace that when it came time to battles we would be drooling for a fight! And for those that don't like that kind of fighting, then give them the option to watch it play out or just auto-resolve. So you basically would have three fighting options/styles.
Good luck devs! I'll be playing and with you to final release rather you take my ideas to heart or not. How long I'll play and how many people I recommend to play the game will depend on how the final game turns out! Fingers crossed you guys nail it! Thanks for all your hard work. I hope it pays off. Peace!

TLDR: It's a good game. I recommend you download it.
Paladins delivers a fun, unique class-based shooter experience that I would definitely recommend.
Contrary to popular belief,
Overwatch Clone:
I do not feel like this is a "Overwatch Clone", while the style and several heroes feel like Overwatch characters, it plays much different.
It embraces more of the shooter aspect of "Class-Based Shooter" than Overwatch. In Overwatch, you have characters using a variety of ways to damage and kill enemies, while most Paladins characters use guns or things seen in other First-Person Shooters. The addition of mounts and other features not seen in Overwatch give it it's own personality.
Characters:
The characters are done very well. Each feels unique and fun, and has a clear-cut playstyle. No character feels the same (except Tyra and Viktor's abilities are pretty similiar, but I digress.) and no one hero is stronger than the other. Each has equal power.
New heroes are released fairly frequently, and that is a good
Abilities:
The abilities are also a strong point in the game, each character's abilities feel different to the other (except the aforementioned Viktor and Tyra.)
I do feel that some abilities should be changed. I feel Lex's Retribution should be changed, as the reward for killing the target is a measly few credits, and you usually will never be able to buy anything from the shop even if you kill all your targets. Using the ability is useless as well, because after your target is killed you get a random one anyway, so using it has no value.
I feel changing it so the reward feels more... rewarding could give much more incentive to play him. (I will add that using the card loadouts you can gain e.g. lifesteal for killing the target, but that isn't part of base Lex and the point still stands.)
Customization:
You can change things like your skin, emote and card loadout. While it adds a nice touch, it should definitely be fleshed out more, because right now there are very little options (but this will probably be changed when the full game is released.)
The card loadouts are done very well, they change the playstyle and gameplay of a character quite a bit. It is easy to get more cards by opening the packs or buying them with the currency (which you get a lot of.)
I hope HiRez expands the customization, because it is overall luke-warm.
Graphics/Art Style:
The art style is very pleasing, looking a lot like a Pixar film. The graphics are good, and even I can run it at a decent framerate and good graphical setting. I think HiRez did a good job on that.
Skill Cap:
It does feel more casual than most other competitive class-based shooters, but it does have the potential to be competitive. The competitive mode is out and, while I haven't played it yet, I think it could blossom into something great.
Gameplay:
The gameplay feels fair and balanced. Fast paced, almost non-stop action. Mounts work well to get you to the fight ASAP, and the abilities compliment the gunplay pretty well. If you find a cooperative team, which seems to happen more than most other games, you can have a fun game.
Overall:
It is a good game, with fun gameplay and graphics. Characters and abilities flow well and compliment gameplay greatly.
While there are some things that I think should be fixed/furthered, like some abilities and customization, the game is great. Would definitely recommend.
PS:
Why wouldn't you get it, it's free.

It is a true sand-box game where the possibilities seem limitless - with the ability to design your own ships or factions, with the existence of a way-too-big tech tree which makes it so your choices actually matter, with multiple legit ways to win the game...  Each game played has been a different experience - although my personal play style seems to keep pushing me toward diplomatic efforts.
The visuals are great, though the some of face animation in cutscenes leaves something to be desired.   The sound is not bad.  But really, it is all about the game play and customizability which will allow this game to have long-lasting value.   And the AI is capable of beating you if you are not paying attention.  This makes the game challenging and fun as you react to decisions made by AI factions.  For this and tremendous customizability (and scale) of the game, I consider the game well worth the value, especially of you are the type that likes to tinker and customize your experience.
It is, of course, not without its faults.
- Now that the campain is released, I find it underwhelming.  I was looking forward to a deeper story and more than a few maps.  I understand that more will be added in the future.  However, the present campaign is thin and lacks the drama that the trailers seemed to promise.
- The game still has a range of random typos, mismatches in what a few techs or improvements say and what they actually do, to go along with the rare crash (rare for me, anyway).
- The cinematic battle viewer is great in concept,... except for when suddenly it choses an angle that isn't showing anything at all.  I guess a camera person fell asleep.
Yes, some of these problems are annoying.  But I think what will make this game endure and makes it well worth the price is that it can be played, replayed, and played with for a long time.  With easy mod creation, it will not be long before there are many quality mods to enhance play.  Because ship parts can animate, the creative among us can create "transforming" ships.  The game is as much about being space emperor as it is about the game within the game (the customization of it).
People looking for a deep engrossing story will be disappointed.  But people looking who like building ships, making designs, making new races, and playing with all your created toys... (people like me) will be able to play this thing for a long long time.

After 40 minuets of ABZU, I'm already giving it a thumbs up, why? Because I like it, I enjoyed it, it's something relaxing instead of intense, it's something that a lot of us needs and wants, not something frustrating but something relaxing and beautiful (like a girlfriend), ABZU could ABZUlutely promise you that.
All the other reviews have been saying ABZU is a beautiful game, a true masterpiece which isn't a game anymore, it's art, yeah yeah it's beautiful alright, but you don't seem to recognize the potential this game has, it's an adventure game where you explore an ocean world with a set course, it's more like clearing a dungeon where you don't need to fight.
In ABZU, you're a diver with a weird cat ears on your helmet (or they're really your ears) and future technology, you dive and swim all the way across the ocean to discover ruins, meet ocean species, find hidden pots which releases more fish and creatures and also revive dead sections of the ocean. With your immortality (or maybe you're just too ugly that the fish doesn't care or the sharks don't wanna eat you), you can ride with or swim with any ocean creatures, don't be freaked out by sharks anymore, they've got a jawful of fish.
There doesn't seem to have a lore in ABZU, but there's definitely something going on, I hope there would be more paths and story hints in the game, where society might be discovered to explain the purpose of ABZU's diver.
Yes, it says "Controller recommended", but I bet a lot of you played hyper light drifter with a mouse and keyboard right? do the same with ABZU then, it's complicated at the start but once you get used to it, it's like playing league, ABZU's controls are simple, hold right click, spam left click, you're swimming, great, E to drift (to do flips and stuff), space to interact and hold shift to ride with the ocean creatures! (sorry to dissapoint you but you don't ride on them, you ride with them.
I can't complain about anything in this game, beautiful animation and graphics, the movement of your little robots (you pick these up across the map, everytime you enter the tri-entrance, they will be confiscated) and so natural, that's a given because it's an ocean map and it could move more naturally, the sound track is amazing and makes you feel spacious, although you might want to watch out for huge fish groups since they might give your fps a sudden bombing.
ABZU isn't just an adventure game, it reminds us of how oceans can become and what did we turn them into, you set off to a journey and your only companions are the ocean neighbours and your little robots, they swim with you, although they don't really do anything (other than cutting coral nets for you), they are cute and loyal which makes you feels like walking with hamsters or rabbits, you can unlock meditation by finding shark statues and look at the creature's habits (they even added in shark hunger on fish).
This is one game that I will give my special attention to, it's made so perfectly that I'm going to stalk this dev for a few months, hoping to see if there are any other games. Buy it if you're a man of fish romance and safe adventure, you set out into a new world of water, fish and beauty, that's all there is and that's what's worth your attention, before no man's sky is out, it would be nice to get this game for some time killing if you have some extra money!

TLDR: It's a good game. I recommend you download it.
Paladins delivers a fun, unique class-based shooter experience that I would definitely recommend.
Contrary to popular belief,
Overwatch Clone:
I do not feel like this is a "Overwatch Clone", while the style and several heroes feel like Overwatch characters, it plays much different.
It embraces more of the shooter aspect of "Class-Based Shooter" than Overwatch. In Overwatch, you have characters using a variety of ways to damage and kill enemies, while most Paladins characters use guns or things seen in other First-Person Shooters. The addition of mounts and other features not seen in Overwatch give it it's own personality.
Characters:
The characters are done very well. Each feels unique and fun, and has a clear-cut playstyle. No character feels the same (except Tyra and Viktor's abilities are pretty similiar, but I digress.) and no one hero is stronger than the other. Each has equal power.
New heroes are released fairly frequently, and that is a good
Abilities:
The abilities are also a strong point in the game, each character's abilities feel different to the other (except the aforementioned Viktor and Tyra.)
I do feel that some abilities should be changed. I feel Lex's Retribution should be changed, as the reward for killing the target is a measly few credits, and you usually will never be able to buy anything from the shop even if you kill all your targets. Using the ability is useless as well, because after your target is killed you get a random one anyway, so using it has no value.
I feel changing it so the reward feels more... rewarding could give much more incentive to play him. (I will add that using the card loadouts you can gain e.g. lifesteal for killing the target, but that isn't part of base Lex and the point still stands.)
Customization:
You can change things like your skin, emote and card loadout. While it adds a nice touch, it should definitely be fleshed out more, because right now there are very little options (but this will probably be changed when the full game is released.)
The card loadouts are done very well, they change the playstyle and gameplay of a character quite a bit. It is easy to get more cards by opening the packs or buying them with the currency (which you get a lot of.)
I hope HiRez expands the customization, because it is overall luke-warm.
Graphics/Art Style:
The art style is very pleasing, looking a lot like a Pixar film. The graphics are good, and even I can run it at a decent framerate and good graphical setting. I think HiRez did a good job on that.
Skill Cap:
It does feel more casual than most other competitive class-based shooters, but it does have the potential to be competitive. The competitive mode is out and, while I haven't played it yet, I think it could blossom into something great.
Gameplay:
The gameplay feels fair and balanced. Fast paced, almost non-stop action. Mounts work well to get you to the fight ASAP, and the abilities compliment the gunplay pretty well. If you find a cooperative team, which seems to happen more than most other games, you can have a fun game.
Overall:
It is a good game, with fun gameplay and graphics. Characters and abilities flow well and compliment gameplay greatly.
While there are some things that I think should be fixed/furthered, like some abilities and customization, the game is great. Would definitely recommend.
PS:
Why wouldn't you get it, it's free.

I came across this game as somewhat of a "recommendation". It looked pretty cute, and it supposedly had a good storyline. So, I picked it up, and I can say I'm quite impressed.
To start off, the game's story revolves around two characters : Efi and Leo. Leo is a man who does nothing but spew lies, and Efi is a young dragon that turns lies into monsters and eats them. Over the course of three chapters, smaller stories involving legends, oddities and supernatural events are laid out in a mostly linear path that prompts the player to interact with objects or NPCs to progress.
The game is strongly story-driven, as the RPG element is fairly lackluster, though the way in which battles are introduced is rather unique and serves the story (the main focus of the game) well. Essentially, Efi is used as a "lie detector" and must defeat and consume manifested lies as Leo solves a "mystery" surrounding the abnormal events. Most points of the game are rather cheery and quirky while others tend to be a bit unnerving, though overall the game gives off a light-hearted tone while delivering a tangible plot. Regardless, I thought the story was pretty solid, which is what makes this game what it is.
As far as art and music go, the artstyle is all very cute-sy and pixel-styled, and my only complaint is that during combat some numbers are difficult to read (though it isn't that large of a problem since battles generally exist to progress plot elements and serve as little more than button mashers). The soundtrack is very nice in my opinion; the themes all fit the art very well and while a bit on the simple side, do generally fit the situation.
So there you have it; LiEat: A small story-driven mini-RPG. Came for an RPG, got a Kinetic Visual Novel.

It can be safely assumed that it is not many people’s dream to devastate the world in a cataclysmic nuclear war. Well, Ronald Reagan and his Soviet counterparts may have been the general exception to that rule. After all, the idea is simply M.A.D. (Mutually Assured Destruction, or a lose/lose scenario), surely? However, that is exactly the situation which the players of DEFCON must face. Inspired both by the 1986 comedy/drama ‘WarGames’, and the 1964 satire ‘Dr. Strangelove’, DEFCON delivers an experience which is both ironically good fun, and ultimately a poignant emotional experience.
The basic premise of DEFCON is that you are a military general, or some other such leader, knuckled down in your secret underground bunker, and for some unknown reason, the diplomatic negotiations have failed, and all-out nuclear war has been declared. You are tasked with defeating your enemy by killing that largest number of civilians using your nuclear arsenal, whilst the enemy does the same. Introversion Software likes to call it ‘losing the least’. Sounds quite cheerful, no? The overall game is very simple right from the get go, and also very small, only taking up about 60mb of hard disk space. However, this does in not in any way dampen the experience.
Controls are easy, simple to use, and quick to learn, and the tutorial levels spell it all out very nicely. However, it is clear from the outset that this is a difficult game to truly master, requiring lots of detailed strategic thinking. In fact, strategic thinking is really the nub of the matter. Many questions will circle round your head while playing, causing constant internal debate. Should I strike first? Should I counter-strike? Should I launch the entire arsenal all in one go or keep a reserve handy? It is all up to you, and your decisions may be crucial in deciding the overall outcome of the war. It is in many respects simply a nuclear combat game of Chess.
You are able to play as one of six continents, North or South America, Africa, Europe, and North or South Asia. There are many different options which can be adjusted to change your game to how you see fit, meaning that the game can be played in a number of different ways, including a nifty mode where the game plays in the background over six-hours; perfect for a dull day at work. Peculiarly, I experienced a quite nasty guilty pleasure when raining down the apocalypse upon the enemy. You can’t help but feel some subconscious guilt whenever there is a direct hit on a major city, and writing flashes up calmly informing you that: ‘London hit, 8.9 million killed’. It really is quite unnerving at certain points, such as when you zoom back to view the entire map, with numerous missiles arching across the sky. I doubt there is another game in existence where you can exterminate more innocent virtual people. However, the game is designed purposefully so that you experience this guilt, and realise how fruitlessly useless and stupid nuclear holocaust actually is.
Graphically, the main game window takes the view of a two dimensional map of the world, an extremely similar layout and style to the 1980’s command screens used by the Pentagon in the film ‘WarGames’. It cannot be understated that the game looks wonderfully cool, feeling crisp, militaristic and clean. The blue tinge to the world and basic graphics add to the 1980’s feel. There are no flashy animations whenever a bomb drops. Instead, the area whites out, just like a radar map, with an ominous dull rumbling noise. The many moving objects leave dotted trails behind them which gradually fade over time. Overall, it almost convinces you sometimes that you really are controlling a superpower’s military armoury.
The sound is really superb, and it is clear that choosing a more sombre and subtle soundtrack was a master stroke. The music is fantastically haunting, and really adds to the overall atmosphere, making me wish there was a lot more of it! All the time in the background, there is the humming of the bunker machinery, radio chatter, distant footsteps, machinery bleeps, and occasionally the quite disturbing sounds of people coughing and crying. By the sounds of it, they could be suffering from acute radiation sickness. It is mostly the sound which really gives the game its poignant side, and shows the real futility of this type of warfare in real life.
Overall, the moral message of DEFCON is similar to both the films of ‘Dr. Strangelove’ and ‘WarGames’. Global Thermonuclear War may seem like a good idea, and is fun as a game, but ultimately in real life it is just plain idiotic. Once you have learned this message, you can really experience the full value of this game. It has wonderful replayability, a genuinely classic format and excellent multiplayer. The only slight negatives are that a longer soundtrack would have been really great, and that if you wanted to play as Australia or the continent of Oceania as it is now known, forget it, as it is an ultimately redundant landmass in game. There is still the slight chance of this being resolved however, as Introversion is continually updating and perfecting the game. These really are only slight quibbles, which if included, would have made the game really superb.
DEFCON is truly a game that shows that it is actually possible to fight in the War Room. Now, how about a nice game of Chess?

It is a true sand-box game where the possibilities seem limitless - with the ability to design your own ships or factions, with the existence of a way-too-big tech tree which makes it so your choices actually matter, with multiple legit ways to win the game...  Each game played has been a different experience - although my personal play style seems to keep pushing me toward diplomatic efforts.
The visuals are great, though the some of face animation in cutscenes leaves something to be desired.   The sound is not bad.  But really, it is all about the game play and customizability which will allow this game to have long-lasting value.   And the AI is capable of beating you if you are not paying attention.  This makes the game challenging and fun as you react to decisions made by AI factions.  For this and tremendous customizability (and scale) of the game, I consider the game well worth the value, especially of you are the type that likes to tinker and customize your experience.
It is, of course, not without its faults.
- Now that the campain is released, I find it underwhelming.  I was looking forward to a deeper story and more than a few maps.  I understand that more will be added in the future.  However, the present campaign is thin and lacks the drama that the trailers seemed to promise.
- The game still has a range of random typos, mismatches in what a few techs or improvements say and what they actually do, to go along with the rare crash (rare for me, anyway).
- The cinematic battle viewer is great in concept,... except for when suddenly it choses an angle that isn't showing anything at all.  I guess a camera person fell asleep.
Yes, some of these problems are annoying.  But I think what will make this game endure and makes it well worth the price is that it can be played, replayed, and played with for a long time.  With easy mod creation, it will not be long before there are many quality mods to enhance play.  Because ship parts can animate, the creative among us can create "transforming" ships.  The game is as much about being space emperor as it is about the game within the game (the customization of it).
People looking for a deep engrossing story will be disappointed.  But people looking who like building ships, making designs, making new races, and playing with all your created toys... (people like me) will be able to play this thing for a long long time.

LiEat is a fun and short game that you may play to pass time. However, do not take this game too seriously or expect the most out of it.
Pros:
~Great graphics in terms of character design and setting
~Lovable character personality
~You become more and more engaged with the game when you get past LiEat Part I
~Cute
~Entertaining, unique, interesting
Cons:
~Very little direction, you will spend a lot if not most of LiEat walking around meaninglessly!
~Ending conditions are awful for LiEat Part III
~Semi-amateurish
~Probably one of the most predictable games I've played in a while
-Indirect Spoilers-
LiEat was very light hearted yet had detective/mystery elements that made you want to play more to see what type of plot twist the game had cooked up for you. Although this is great for early-midgame of each part, you find yourself disappointed as the endings are pretty much the most obvious paths you could even imagine. Hell, red herrings are supposed to lead the player to believe that one character is the culprit, only an UNEXPECTED person to be the crime doer! This game doesn't do that. Also the ending condition for LiEat III was petty. Basically the game forces you to check around with little direction for a clue, consequently the player rechecks a lot of thing. If you check a certain thing more than once, bam, you get a bad ending without the slightest warning.
-end spoiler-
Despite the disappointing endings, I recommend this game because it entertained me most of the time, which you know, is the point of games! You'll really love the characters, and it will probably make you smile. The story is interesting and makes you want to know more.

I don't generally write reviews, but I thought that Galactic Civilizations III deserved one.
While the game is a considerable amount of fun, there are certain downsides to it. For instance, the ideology system is vary poorly balanced. To have every planet and station within your sphere of influence automatically switch over to your side, is very heavily over-powered. It took me no longer than twenty minutes on my last run through to control almost 100% of the map. And throughout the whole time, I did not so much as even build an additional scout ship (beyond what you start off with of course). Secondly, there are bugs. But this is early access after all. So if you're willing to buy, than you need to take that into consideration. In my case, I have an issue with the diplomacy menu where the music decides to cut out and menu refuses to move. Lastly, the AI still seems to have an edge over the player. For whatever reason the AI colonizes every planet within reach in a rather insane amount of time. No matter how much I would spend on production I could not get my population to expand fast enough to start a reasonable colony.
Now I should mention the positives. First and foremost, the graphics are remarkable. At full settings the game is beautiful. The video game score is also top notch. Ship customization is also a great tool to tailor the game more to your liking. And with the developers working actively on Galactic Civilzations, it is my hope that the negatives I mention get fixed. Nonetheless, I will still play the series as I am a rather huge Gal Civ fan. So I recommend this game to anyone whose willing to overlook the minor inconveniences, and just have some sort of fun.

Having freshly finished the Witcher Enhanced edition and being thrilled by its mechanics and features I was very eager to start playing the Witcher 2.
I can't really describe what a huge disappointment it was. Although at the beggining the nice graphics (and the main characters love interest nicer body :P) and the immersive environment (making you really feel the way you would probably feel in a military camp or a dungeon) I was disappointed once actual combat and gameplay started. Actually the graphics and the environment might be the only positive factors in this game.
The EPIC combat system from the Witcher is gone, replaced by some standard and comparably  mediocre one in which you just chain right clicks after left clicks, while aiming a bit randomly, seeing that there is no crosshair or sth to help you aim and there is no more group fighting style. Where the Witcher was a bit to easy to play even on the highest difficulty, the WItcher 2 is too difficult, complicated and comparably frustrating to play even in normal mode. For some reason the makers even totally changed the mechanics and key bindnings, so that there is no common link between Witcher and Witcher 2 playing styles. Now, instead of wrecking enemies with your mutant strength and agility, you just jump around trying not to get hit and hitting the enemies from behind, not even being able to defeat a shieldbearer head on, although in the ridiculous killing animations you are flinging bodies around as if you were Hercules. A bunch of cool sounding extra combat moves have been added, like manual parrying and arrow deflection, ripostes, and knife throwing, non of which are really usefull, seeing that you have no effective way of handling groups of enemies in order to enable you to have time to specifically time your moves to deflect and riposte. And of course the extreme realism of planintg traps IN FRONT of the enemy, who then just takes the bait and steps into a (not even conceiled!) apparatus is beyond me!
Now you have to meditate to even drink potions (like telling you to drink while you sleep so that you don't get thirsty during the rest of the day), making potions useless in combat and various situations, except if you "somehow" already know what you are going to encounter. A weight limit has been added, as well as the possibility to pick up whatever items you want, culminating in a typical Skyrim situation of "HOLY F*CK HOW AM I GOING TO HAUL ALL THIS TO A MERCHANT?!?!". You can get overencumbered by the end of the introduction with no merchant available anywhere durign the introduction and part of the next chapter.
The story process, decision making options and their impact are even more obscure and iritating than the ones in Witcher 1. Having, as said, finished the Witcher while helping the elves and dwarves and getting the King to grant them equal rights, I imported my save to Witcher 2 and got my armor and weapons (now ofc nerfed down so you actually have to get diferent equipment during the game, that is logical). Now I find myself being the lackey and bodyguard of a King who promptly followed up on ostracizing and fighting the elves and dwarves, assuming daring commando missions to slay groups of other humans just because he sais so (Witchers are supposed to be monster slayers -_-)  and having a negative attitude and killing elves without getting a chance to do otherwise at the beggining.
The achievements are also a joke, being granting for difficult tasks like drinking a potion and finishing quests you have to finish anyway!
The only reason I OBJECTIVELY give this game 5/10 ('cause subjectively it would have been even less!) is that it still holds up with some not too bad RPG's that are around on the market. I seriously hope that they will add good old vanilla Witcher stuff in Witcher 3, else I won't even bother buying it.

After 40 minuets of ABZU, I'm already giving it a thumbs up, why? Because I like it, I enjoyed it, it's something relaxing instead of intense, it's something that a lot of us needs and wants, not something frustrating but something relaxing and beautiful (like a girlfriend), ABZU could ABZUlutely promise you that.
All the other reviews have been saying ABZU is a beautiful game, a true masterpiece which isn't a game anymore, it's art, yeah yeah it's beautiful alright, but you don't seem to recognize the potential this game has, it's an adventure game where you explore an ocean world with a set course, it's more like clearing a dungeon where you don't need to fight.
In ABZU, you're a diver with a weird cat ears on your helmet (or they're really your ears) and future technology, you dive and swim all the way across the ocean to discover ruins, meet ocean species, find hidden pots which releases more fish and creatures and also revive dead sections of the ocean. With your immortality (or maybe you're just too ugly that the fish doesn't care or the sharks don't wanna eat you), you can ride with or swim with any ocean creatures, don't be freaked out by sharks anymore, they've got a jawful of fish.
There doesn't seem to have a lore in ABZU, but there's definitely something going on, I hope there would be more paths and story hints in the game, where society might be discovered to explain the purpose of ABZU's diver.
Yes, it says "Controller recommended", but I bet a lot of you played hyper light drifter with a mouse and keyboard right? do the same with ABZU then, it's complicated at the start but once you get used to it, it's like playing league, ABZU's controls are simple, hold right click, spam left click, you're swimming, great, E to drift (to do flips and stuff), space to interact and hold shift to ride with the ocean creatures! (sorry to dissapoint you but you don't ride on them, you ride with them.
I can't complain about anything in this game, beautiful animation and graphics, the movement of your little robots (you pick these up across the map, everytime you enter the tri-entrance, they will be confiscated) and so natural, that's a given because it's an ocean map and it could move more naturally, the sound track is amazing and makes you feel spacious, although you might want to watch out for huge fish groups since they might give your fps a sudden bombing.
ABZU isn't just an adventure game, it reminds us of how oceans can become and what did we turn them into, you set off to a journey and your only companions are the ocean neighbours and your little robots, they swim with you, although they don't really do anything (other than cutting coral nets for you), they are cute and loyal which makes you feels like walking with hamsters or rabbits, you can unlock meditation by finding shark statues and look at the creature's habits (they even added in shark hunger on fish).
This is one game that I will give my special attention to, it's made so perfectly that I'm going to stalk this dev for a few months, hoping to see if there are any other games. Buy it if you're a man of fish romance and safe adventure, you set out into a new world of water, fish and beauty, that's all there is and that's what's worth your attention, before no man's sky is out, it would be nice to get this game for some time killing if you have some extra money!

Binding of Isaac may seem like a really simple top down RPG shooter, but trust me when I say that's just a front. If you can look past the cartoonish art style and simplistic look then you'll see a really expansive game with tonnes to find and do.
Now first things first: this game is hard. You will spend a lot of your time dying, dying and dying again. If you're gonna whine about a difficult unforgiving game, then don't get this. When you die, that's game over. You start again at the beginning with nothing.
Along your journey you'll find a total over 235 items which upgrade your character. I'd say this is what actually makes the game shine, all the items are randomized so every time you play through it, you'll get different items which change how you play. A really nice touch is that the items also change your character's appearance, which is a visually pleasing change.
One issue I have with this is that there's usually no indication as to what the items actually do. Unless you have a wiki open whilst you're playing, you're gonna have a bad time. It would have been nice if they at least included an in-game encyclopaedia.
Because all the items are randomized, a lot of this game is down to luck which decides whether or not you actually have a successful game which kinda sucks. Overall, considering it's really cheap and a fun game, it gets a 6 out of 10 so pick it up if you have the money!
