There is a lot of hate towards this game. Part of it is deserved, but the rest not so much. I think it´s good game for discounted price. I bought Deluxe edition on Humble Store for 23€ and I am more than satisfied with what I got for the price, even if the game itself has some serious issues.
I liked the most the atmosphere of the game, which is unique. The only reason why I collected all the collectibles was because I loved just to walk/drive around in this big open world with a beautiful design. There is a lot of details around the city and its inhabitants, beautiful rain effects and the great soundtrack also helps a lot. I loved the fact that you can travel by boat to all areas which I have never seen before in open world game like this.
The story is ok. Nothing breathtaking or worth replaying, but it´s not boring or short, so I cannot complain in this department. The same with gameplay. There is A LOT of content. And yes, A LOT of it is kind of simple and repetitive, because majority of optional/side missions are "old-school", just go steal the truck and get it back or clear this and that warehouse full of enemies and so on, but I enjoyed it. It was sort of nostalgic, because it reminded me first GTA games.
Performance is good. I have 970 GTX and with maxed out settings in 1920x1080 I did not experience any framerate drops or crashing at all.
Now, let´s get to negatives.
First of all, a lot of textures are low-res for some reason. I can find nice little poster with high-res detailed texture and then there are walls and whole grounds with textures looking like we got back in time to 2010. It´s really weird and they didn´t fix it after 6 months, so they probably don´t care about this, but this texture quality is ridiculous for big AAA title from late 2016.
Second, there is blurry image as ****. Mafia III is not the only game with this issue, but this one is really the worst case. Luckily for us PC gamers, we can use Reshade/Sweetfx and its lumasharpen does the job quite well and removes the blurry image. In the end graphics look quite good after applying this effect, but that doesn´t change the fact that developers did something horribly wrong and are delivering big mess to customers who have to fix it on their own.
Collectibles are almost all pointless, because you get pretty much no reward. Like you can see enemies behind the walls, but you can get this ability another way, so no point in collecting hundreds of fuses.
After 6 months there is still A LOT of bugs left, although it is nothing game-breaking. Usually just some graphical issues as floating objects in the air and flickering shadows. Or issues with completed side missions showing up as uncompleted on the map and some achievements not checking out as completed. Also I collected all the collectibles and still it is not showing as 100%, which is weird.
Overall, I give this game 7/10. I have enjoyed it, but a lot of potential for a truly amazing game has been wasted here.
I can recommend it to those who can enjoy somewhat simple and repetitive gameplay, don´t need always the best graphics and are not interested in buying this only because they liked previous two games in the series. Especially the last one could be a big problem why so many people are butthurt. This is not anymore that classic Italian mafia story we are used to. This is just an ordinary revenge tale with mafia background.

If you are reading this review before I change my avatar (it may happen sooner or later) you will understand how much I love this game. I will be writing an honest review though, focusing on PRO and CON aspects of the game.
PRO
- Re-playability: you will never play this game the same way twice! Every stage of the storyline offers you a great variety of choices that will highly influence the world around you. You will be facing hard decisions, since the very beginning to the very ending of the game.
- Combat system: the combat system of The Witcher 2 is particular and interesting. You will be carrying two swords: a steel one for human targets and a silver blade for monsters. You need to decide which sword to use depending on the enemy you will be facing. In addition to this there is a number of tools, traps, ranged weapons you can use, potions you can drink that have to be prepared before the battle. Depending on the enemy you must, then, think at the perfect strategy to defeat it!
- Customization: upon leveling up you gain one point you can spend on one of the four perk paths: Witcher, Swordsmanship, Magic and Alchemy. You have to complete the first one to unlock the other three (which is not a problem). You can add a perk in every path regardless of the initial choice, but the more you advance in a path, the better abilities you will gain, it is another decision you have to take! :)
- Graphics: playing the Witcher 2 at max graphic renders you utterly speechless, the details, the motion blur, the texturing and modeling is almost flawless considering it is a 2011 game.
- Arena mode: this mode offers you lots of new hours of gameplay. You will have to kill waves of enemies, and with every wave completed you gain perk points and currency to improve yourself in order to face the next wave. Score, then, can be registered to compare it with other players.
CON
- Diffuculties gap: the easiest difficulty may make you finish the game even without the need of adding perks. Almost every enemy can be killed by normal sword slashes, while the hardest mode is an incredibly challenging mode. There is not a real midpoint.
- Identical NPCs: hardly you will find NPCs with their own unique features, apart from the characters you will interact with during the main storyline. Sometimes clothes and outfits are different, but the face model is the same. There are few base models being used in different towns (poor woman, poor man, noble woman, noble man, dwarf, male elf, female elf etc).
I definitely recommend this game, especially now that The Witcher 3 will be released next year. It is an amazing way to get familiar with the Witcher world, lore and system!

It's not every time I review a game, but I thought the need to review this game was high! Bus Simulator 16 is set in the town of Sunny Springs. Not only are you a bus driver, but you have to deal with a variety of events that happen around you!
The driving and stability of the bus is relatively easy. I'm currently using a Logitech G27 and I'm able to turn the steering wheel with no problem. However, I feel it can be quite stiff sometimes, but I'm sure this will be improved.
The passengers are amazing. You get a variety of different talks whilst driving your bus, from calling in sick to work, talking to fellow passengers etc. Other than when I give passengers their ticket, they say 'Thank you dear'. There are also other events including asking a passenger to move so you can close the doors, helping a wheelchair user onto the bus where you may need to get out of your seat and operate it manually or press a button at the cab, turning the air con/heating up or down to the passengers' wish or even dealing with drunk passengers. Pedestrians also relatively behave probably, I do get the occasional event where a passenger walks out in front of me at a crossing and your current drive would end immediately.
There are also other events including fixing a jammed door, where you need to get out of your seat and manually close the door.
The graphics overall are pretty good. I've been hearing reports about the textures glitching out and turning to grey, however I have not been getting this problem. A feature I do like is when it's raining and the trees blow around. Unfortunately, when it is raining, you don't get any rain effects on the windscreen which was quite a disappointment. There are wipers, but there is no point in really using these.
The AI's behaviour in-game is very good, they will react to your indicators very well, like when you are pulling out of a bus stop, the car behind you will stop and let you out. There does seem to be a glitch where if you are sat in the cockpit, you won't be able to see the AI's lights (indicators, brake lights) but you will be able to see them from outside of the bus. This might explain to some people why they have been crashing into the back of AI cars, which I have done a couple of times.  AI will also behave probably when at traffic lights or junctions, so the developers have done a good job on coding the AI vehicles!
The FPS I get in-game is relatively good to keep it stable. I get around 40-50FPS overall when driving around or walking about in my office/garage. I have been looking at the reviews where some people have put a thumbs down because of the poor FPS they get in-game. I seem to be one of the lucky ones where I don't get any FPS problems and can play the game with no problem. However, I'm sure for those who are getting problems that there will be a patch relatively soon.
Overall, I believe Bus Simulator 16 is a great simulator and is much better than the previous bus simulator I had, which was OMSI 2, which had no end of glitches, crashes and bad in-game optimization etc. It's not every day you get a good Bus Simulator like this, probably one of the best to date. There may be a few glitches and bugs there and there, but let's be grateful that we have a good Bus Simulator!

First thing that hits you when you run this game is a big happy feeling right from the initial screen.  This continues throughout the game, thanks to lots of warm-hearted animations and little background flourishes that breathe life into the environment.
The music perfect matches the gameplay, it seems to get you into a puzzle solving rhythm and spur you along. Sound effects are well rounded and never annoying.
I liked the purity of the control mechanic. The challenges posed by the game purely come from the playful and challenging level design.  This makes it easy to pickup which maxmises its potential audience.  So many games get this wrong and end up complicating the controls (e.g. multiple action buttons) which just puts players off from the start.
What addicted me most was trying to get a perfect score. I was never satisfied with simply completing a level, I felt the need to prove myself to the game by sussing out the optimal route!
One of the puzzle themes is ensuring you use specific coloured sides of the cube to squash some enemies. This is nice as it gets you thinking spatially in 3 dimensions which feels like a mini-workout for the brain.
The whole experience is rounded off with nice soft damped player and camera motions.

In this day and age a pretty decent stealth game is a rarity! So I hope no devs feel offended by my description of Aragami as "pretty decent".
The game consists as a linear sequence of missions, or levels. Each level is also somewhat linear as you have a single objective at any time but the path to do so is not a linear path. The levels have good sizes, full of curves, obstacles, explorable corners and well place guards. It feels nice and rewarding to traverse. You can find a higher ground, scout the place, study the guards movements, make a plan etc. All that stealthy good stuff!
The third person perspective works nicely with the choice for the large open areas the designers decided for the levels. Large open areas, by the way, are usually a problem for stealth games but it works surprisingly well here. Probably because the detection system is extremely well signaled. There are 'approximately' two levels if light: light and shadow. You are visible in one and invisible in the other. I used quotation marks in 'approximately' because there are some very bright spots here and there but they seem to be their own thing independent of the lighting system, and they function like localized obstacles. These lights make you very visible and drain your magic, which I'll talk about later. But my point is this simplification of detection system is a good thing. It removes the dubiousness of detection system and creates a gameplay more purely about stealth, and keeps these large open areas from being overwhelming to the player, because guards can have line of sight from anywhere. Dubious could work if stealth weren't the main gameplay element, so you could try, fail and start shooting your way out, but that's not what Aragami is going for.
Another interesting mechanic is the teleportation thing, which I'll just call blink in reference to Dishonored because that's pretty much what it is. You can blink only to shadow regions, but you can also create small patches of shadow that disappear very quickly. And these two mechanic play extremely well with the other mechanics in the game! It creates so many possible solutions to traverse the environments. You can't spam these blinks and shadows at will, because they drain magic. Magic restores in a matter of seconds while in shadow, so the purpose is to just keep the player from spamming shadow and blink all the way through the levels, and plan ahead of time where you want to land.
There is a skill tree where you can buy some abilities. Upgrade system in stealth games can be game breaking. The level designer has no way of knowing how the player invested his points. I don't think this happened here though. There are few skills to choose from and they seem to work well within the game and the levels seem to not be broken by assumptions on what my character is.
The plot is the most disappointing aspect of the game. It's like all the fantasy cliche mumble jumble got thrown into a blender. You got your light vs dark, mastery of the elements, the talismans, spirits etc. It would've been forgivable if these devices were used to tell an interesting story but the plot is also underwhelming and predictable.
There are noticeable lacks of polish here and there. Since the movement mechanics give you so much freedom it's not surprising to find you can find ways outside a level or get stuck in uneven terrain, but uncommon enough to be forgivable. The most annoying problem I've found is the ragdoll of an enemy falling down ledges. Specially archers, as they stand close to edges and they always fall down alerting others. This should have been addressed, in my opinion. Either by tweaking the ragdoll system or the takedown process when near edges or rethinking the whole hiding body as a skill and implementing a dragging feature from the start so that the player could manually hold the bodies to keep them from falling down.
All in all I really enjoyed Aragami.

Overall I liked 3 Stars of Destiny.   It is an oldschool style rpg with a mix of interesting characters and some humor.   The combat system is solid, it has good level design, lots of secrets, challenges, and achievements. With that being said, if you do not like snes style rpgs, there's probably not much I can do to convince you to like it.  You either like this style of game, or you hate it.  Nothing I'm typing here will change your mind if you hate RPG maker games. Please do note that unlike most reviews, I have actually completed the game.  I would say it takes a good 25-30 hours on regular difficulty.  On to the details...
The characters are unique without spoiling anything.   There are some interesting ones and later in the game you get to split up the party into 3 groups so choices do matter.  There's often funny banter between characters.  Gameplay is pretty standard for an RPG.  You will need to grind a bit to get some levels, but combat is pretty fun.  Money will be in short supply until late in the game, so grinding isn't too bad or painful.  There are also achievements and optional fights that are quite challenging.  The dungeons, both indoor and outdoor are pretty massive.   There are TONS of secrets and a lot of achievements and the game has replayability if you're inclined.   You can try a speedrun, beat it on hard mode, find all hidden areas, etc.   Also, if you do decide to get the game, without being a spoiler, be sure to check out the swamp area fully.  There is a missable character and dungeon if just blast through it hastily!
The one negative point I would mention about 3 stars is the plot.  I will admit the plot is weak and somewhat illogical at times.  I would say that the later levels feel almost surrealist in nature as far as the theme of different level areas.  If Salvador Dali created an RPG maker game, this might come close to it!   Due to this, I would say that I really prefer Aldorlea's other massive RPG, the Book of Legends, over 3 stars. TBoL has a more cohesive plot and a ton of characters so I would recommend you try that one first.
So what makes 3 stars worth it if the plot isn't that spectacular?    The gameplay and characters are both good and it's a very solid game overall.  Interaction between the characters is pretty funny at times and that keeps things interesting. Great dungeons, fun combat, some tough optional bosses give it the core of a good RPG.  Add in lots of replayability and steam achievements and trading cards and it's a good buy.  If you like Aldorlea RPGs, it's solid and a lot of fun.  If you're on the fence about this one, I'd say try The Book of Legends first for a more cohesive plot.   You can also download a playable demo of both games from Aldorlea's site that will let you play the full game for an hour, just to get an idea of the characters and style.  Hope this helps!

It's classic Orcs Must Die! except... you have to earn back all the traps from the last 2.  So for a good while you're going to have terribly useless traps and have a hell of a time defending your rift.   But once you start getting higher in level and unlocking classic traps and upgrading them (which is new and a nice touch) it will start to feel more like classic Orcs Must Die.  The addition of new characters is also really nice.  Each one has it's limitations and strengths which is required really for any sort of multiplayer team game.  The community is pretty good not too terribly toxic.  You will find some players are more helpful than others but even when you lose you still get XP and will work your way to the higher difficulties and ability to unlock more exotic traps.  If you liked the other 2 Orcs Must Die! and you can muster the patience to slog through the grind Orcs Must Die! Unchained is fun.

Memories... This game evokes many. I first played Final Fantasy VII in 1998 since I was late to the PSX party; it was the entire reason I made it a point to purchase a Playstation in the first place. I had just turned 15 and had the entire summer ahead of me. This was probably my tenth playthrough of FFVII and the first time I've touched the game since 2004.
I was excited to sit through the intro as Midgar slowly comes into view again and we gradually see the full expanse of the mako megapolis in all of its glory, spouting geysers of planet energy into the air miles above the upper plate. Seeing Aerith's face slowly appear on my screen reminded me of an angsty, heartbroken 15 year old version of myself that could never forgive the game developers for doing what they did, even though what they did is probably what cemented this game in my mind as one of the all-time greats. They got me emotionally invested, which probably isn't very hard to do with a 15 year old - let's be real. There are critics everywhere and I respect their opinions on why FFVII is flawed - but I'm here to share why I think it's great and has withstood the test of time.
Let's start out with the setting. Inconsistent? Maybe a little. Fun and interesting? Absolutely. Midgar (especially at the time of the game's release) was unlike anything ever seen in a video game before. It was dark, gritty and full of danger. Your capital city isn't supposed to be crawling with monsters and infested by extremely unsavory folk at every turn. I mean EVERY turn. We aren't talking your staple renegade rogues and bandits, either. We're talking a group of eco-terrorists, a brothel with all kinds of sexual deviants, and a Kingpin pimp with the rule over the most lustrious town in the slums. Not to mention you have ShinRa's hitman shadowing you in the very early stages of the game: Reno. Most of this was unheard of in video games, especially a game that garnered as much attention as Final Fantasy VII did and still does. Clearly, there was a good formula at the start.
Leaving Midgar, you begin traveling to other towns which are typically much smaller and far less populated as well as more peaceful... if they haven't been ravaged by ShinRa, Inc. Some favorite locations for me personally, in no particular order include:
Fort Condor -- It's small and there's hardly anything going on there. Two people to talk to, but this place first gave me the initial sense of desperation people feel towards ShinRa (outside of AVALANCHE and some other Midgar residents) as they fight to protect the near-extinct Condors, one of which happens to be nesting atop the Mako Reactor built there.
Costa del Sol -- Swing by and have a Tropical Nights at the bar! Costa del Sol was the first town in Final Fantasy VII I felt like I could relax in (the short run-in with Hojo aside). Finally I seemed to be out of ShinRa's grasp for a little bit and had some chill time. The music and ambience of this town is the first like it I really got to experience in such detail; it felt like a fun, albeit short, reprieve for the crew. Everyone split up and gave you the opportunity to have brief dialogue with each member of your party.
Nibelheim -- One of the creepiest towns outside of Silent Hill. You walk into Nibelheim and you automatically know something's wrong (outside of it just being there alone since it should be ash). The townsfolk are all obviously hiding something and just simply either chuckle at you or demand that you leave. Nibel Mansion is one of the most unsettling places around, although I think they could've done better with enemy choices for this location to expand upon that, the music is chilling as you venture deeper and deeper into the mansion to try and uncover the mysteries it hides.
Wutai -- It's like Beijing and Kyoto got mashed together hundreds of years ago with pretty awesome results. Wutai is one of the biggest locations you can visit outside of Midgar and even has a large mountain - Da Chao - in which you can participate in a sidequest to rid yourself of a slimy pimp and settle an old score once and for all. The Pagoda is my favorite. Influenced by Bruce Lee's 'Game of Death' there are five floors for the spunky young ninja Yuffie to fight her way up in 1 on 1 combat before meeting the Grandmaster in a deadly fight for supremacy, and pretty good rewards.
I like most locations in FFVII and could keep talking about them for awhile, but let's skip all that. Next, I want to talk about some COMBAT.
FFVII sports the ATB System which allows you to increase or decrease the speed of battle at your leisure - personally, I have to go full throttle in games like this, but to each their own. Materia is engaging but not so comlex that it will make you walk away scratching your head in frustration. It's fun to level up and see new spells get unlocked as well as find new Materia. My major gripe with Materia is that the stat adjustments (some would give you -02% HP, for example), were pretty inconsequential; especially with the introduction of HP / MP Plus Materia. I like the cause and effect game and trying to work through it more.  There are several different Materia types which I'll break down here:
Magic (Green) Materia: Magic Materia covers all of the elements such as Fire, Lightning and Ice. There are a number of others as well. You start off with Fire, Bolt and Ice as the basic spells of these Materia and as you win battles, your Materia basically gains experience as well and will eventually evolve to its next stage and unlock a higher tiered spell for most. This was very interesting as in other games it just seemed to be either done at a random level some character would learn a new spell for the most part - FFIII for SNES being one of the exceptions also.
Summon (Red) Materia: Ever feel like calling forth a primordial beast from the depths of the netherworld to wreak havoc upon your enemies? Yeah? Well, you should probably get mental help. Summons are bad♥♥♥♥♥incarnations that are... summoned, and do heavy damage to all enemies. Most of these guys are elemental based as well and they range from an Ice Queen to the Lord of the Underworld all the way up to a mecha-Godzilla looking Dragon that blasts your enemies from outer space with the force of a nuclear bomb. I can dig it.
Command (Yellow) Materia: This Materia is very versatile in that it enhances a character's actions or unlocks new actions for the character utilizing the materia. For example, throw Double-Cut on Tifa and she will attack twice in a row with a physical attack instead of the normal one time. Sense Materia allows you to view the HP/Status of an enemy at any time when used, and you can even use your Gil as a weapon to hurl at your opponents - the more you throw, the more damage is done.
Support (Blue) Materia: Also very useful, allowing you to cast basic single targetting spells on all enemies and even allowing you to Steal when you perform a certain attack that you have the Materia linked with.
Independent (Pink) Materia: Covering your allies is always useful if you have someone who can take a lot of punishment. Some of this Materia is good and useful early in the game - later on, it feels pretty broken though. I would've liked to have done without.
I did get Materia Master on this playthrough and it was very gratifying for me, personally. Though I will warn you, it is time consuming and there are a few Materia that you can miss and if you do: you will not get the achievement on that playthrough.
Combat is fast and exciting for awhile and if you're a gaming masochist like me, the Battle Arena at Gold Saucer can be really fun, especially if you go there at lower levels. Some of the Materia combos just make this game busted at higher levels. I think Ruby and Emerald Weapons (the super bosses of this game) each got two to three hits on me before I annhilated them.

This is a fantastic little puzzler and an incredible bargain at the price.
On first glance I was skeptical, as the cute pixelated graphics and seemingly simple gameplay (directing a cube around an isometric grid) suggested nothing more than a time waster that I'd finish in a couple of hours.  No chance!
Thankfully, the difficulty curve steps up gradually, eventually becoming rock hard, through the introduction of limited moves, different coloured sides which must be used to squish matching coloured plants, mined explosives, time limits, porcupine cubes that take you out along with other guard sentries etc.
Gameplay and controls (arrow keys) are really easy to pick up, but as each level becomes more and more intricate, you need to carefully plan and experiment to solve.  Getting past the next level feels really rewarding, while the pop synth soundtrack is also great addition.  Can't recommend this game more highly!

Buying this game and expecting a quality game is like buying a copy of the Star Wars Holiday Special and expecting a quality Star Wars movie.
So many things wrong. I'll start with the problem no one else talks about: The prices of everything are almost grotesquely detached from reality (a surplus M1911 costs $7,000 - that's $50,000 adjusted for inflation. The good guns would cost more than a Rolls-Royce). If I waltzed on into Harry's gun shop in Mafia II and he demanded $3,000,000 and seven virgin sacrifices in exchange for a pocket knife, it would be less jarring. Oh and, In Mafia III, you buy all your guns from a racial stereotype that drives a van.
Pros:
John Donovan is one of my favorite video game characters ever. He's like Zuko from The Last Airbender movie: Every other character may be a steaming dog turd ensconced in a dumpster fire of a movie, but somehow he winds up being the one really quality character.
You get to meet Vito Scalleta again, but he doesn't do much and mainly just wallows in his own saddness. You can give him a happy ending he missed at the end of Mafia II. Happy ending could be literal or metaphorical, because I would enthusiatically felliate the god of video game refunds if it meant I got the time and money back that I wasted on this game.
Cons:
1) ->>>>>>>Extremely repetitive Gameplay.<<<<<<<---- It's ridiculous. You have been warned.
2) All the characters except Donovan suck and are head-bangingly uncreative (a drunk, lazy irishman is a big character, for example). Also, everything about them is very predictable. It's like watching Jurassic World: Whenever a character is introduced, you can tell within two seconds if they're going to get eaten by a dinosaur (or, ya know, hate-murdered by Lincoln Clay).
4) This game has zero plot twists and none of the characters have any nuance. They could have hired M. Night Shyamalan to make this video game, and it would probably have turned out better.
5) There's a beautiful city ... and nothing cool happens with it. It's just a useless background.
6) You can't really rob stores (robbing stores was like my favorite thing to do in Mafia II).
7) You can't buy clothes and the few clothing customization options suck.
8) You can only carry two guns at a time. If you played Mafia II, imagine playing that game with only 2 guns. If you want to switch guns, you have to call Cassandra and a racial stereotype will instantly drive up in a van carrying enough firepower to overthrow the Panamanian government.
9) The guns have stupid, fictional names (An AK-47 is a "Pasadena" for Christ's sake). So, I guess that means famed Soviet weapons maker Mikhail Kalashnivok is an American from California now.
10) Mafia III is just a basic revenge plot meant to justify the mindless, repetitive slaughter you get to experience. It's like Man on Fire in video game form: You get to sit back, relax, and watch♥♥♥♥♥♥die, and the plot is just there for it to all make just enough 0sense.
11) You can't be "wanted" and escaping the police is stupid easy. However, you can't pick up police guns, so if you get into a protracted shootout you will run out of ammo and die.
12) If you die and forgot to bank your cash, you lose half of it. To bank your cash, you have to drive all the way across the map and click on a safe in a basement OR assign the first few districts you earn to Cassandra to get her "concierge service."
14) Spoiler alert (not like you should care though): Joe's dead. Nothing interesting happens with his story. For some reason, his killers all live in New Bordeux and you can track down this gaggle of idiot henchmen and kill them 1-by-1 in an extremely repetitive manner.
15) Spoiler alert (but not really because it is so predictable): The game ends with you killing Sal Marcano after a shootout at that giant, idiotic casino he spends the entire game failing to build. The shootout is surprisingly short and not that epic.
16) Spoiler alert (but, not really): The lamest villain I have ever seen in any video game is that Cuban hitman dude. There's a big cutscene where this skilled Cuban hitman is sent to kill you. Basically, you go into his little circle on the map and, 30 seconds later, he drives up with like 3 henchmen. Shoot all 4 and, boom, that entire section of the story is instantly complete.

It has almost everything I was looking for in a Bus driving simulation game out of the box.
+ easy controls: every switch on the bus panel is highlighted when holding RMB
+ big living city: every car and pedestrian around you is simulated
+ you can walk around in the city, inside your bus and drink a virtual cup of coffee
+ believable passenger behaviour: mumbling, complaining, etc
+ cashier mode: you do the math, but keep at eye on the clock, because it's ticking for the next stop
+ easier to start with than OMSI
+ manage your own bus company, hire drivers, buy more buses, create routes
+ company progress, leveling & unlockable buses, decals, advertisements, city districts
+ good steering wheel support
+ modding perspective: custom buses, customizable city, textures, decals
- performance. High graphic settings are laggish for me now, I have to play on medium with anti-aliasing and it runs well.
- no button for centering the camera view, it would come in handy when using a steering wheel
- some people have reported that keyboard & mouse controls are not that great (but I am using a steering wheel anyway)
1. I created a new route and was driving it. I missed a turn and didn't notice that for a minute, heard passengers saying something like "- Are you sure we are on the right bus? - Yes, I checked the map, it is the shortest route". Then I looked at the map and realized I took the wrong turn and GPS was showing me that I should make a very long detour I couldn't do in time anyway. So I turned around in a nearest convenient place (they should have fined me for that though), but I made it in time to the next bus stop.
2. Invalid passengers, when they ask for help, you have to get out of the bus and pull the ramp for them to get into the bus.
3. An ambulance drove the street on my lane, I had to turn a little more to the right to give way. I haven't seen this kind of thing in other games.
I wish accidents were more realistic, not just fining the player, but with all serious consequences like in the real world.
I am still not sure if creating custom city maps is possible with the current modding tools. Only customizing the existing one is allowed, afaik.
I have a feeling this game should have been delayed a little bit more. In perspective, this game can make the best bus simulator once all performance / stability problems are fixed. I'm really enjoying the game so far.

Plain and simple, this is the bus driving game I've been waiting for. What gets me excited about playing this game are the little things that do a lot to the immersion: Passengers running late, waiving at you in hopes you won't take off without them; traffic that doesn't constantly crash into you or each other but yield when you indicate that you are about to set off; jammed doors or passengers blocking doors from closing; handicapped passengers in need of a ramp; events like dynamic construction sites or an ambulance with wailing sirens, etc..
Further, Bus Simulator 16 gives you incentives to drive safely as you gain more reputation with your passengers when you do not drive like a maniac. You can if you want to, but it will hurt the rate of your progression (and your economy):
Like Euro Truck Simulator 2, Bus Simulator 16 additionally has a management simulation mechanic which lets you buy new busses, hire drivers to generate additional revenue, customize your vehicles and even create all the routes on your own. These things (including new districts) are unlocked step by step as your reputation grows.
If you have played other public transportation simulators before then you quickly learn the controls. The tutorial is also a good addition in explaining all the important elements. Handling and getting the bus to move is easier in Bus Simulator 16 than for example OMSI 2. Therefore, hardcore OMSI fans might get a little dissatisfied as mastering your vehicle is way simpler.
The five available districs are rich in variety and the city is actually bigger than it seems when looking at the map. Unfortunately, the tool for creating routes does not give you any degree of freedom when it comes to choosing which road you want to use, resulting in odd and annoying routing in some cases.
Further, and despite Bus Simulator 16 being neatly polished for a simulation game, it is quite heavy on performance. So if you do not have a very 'potent' computer you might get really poor framerates.
Nonetheless, this game got me motivated and hooked right from the start. I hope for additional features for the route creation tool and performance improvements but apart from that I consider my 25 bucks well spent.

can I recommend this Bus simulator, well YES and NO.
And let me start by saying that if you consider buying this or some other bus simulator then I would highly recommend you to buy bus and cable car simulator instead..
Well let me review Bus simulator 16 first, it is actual quite good and have allot of good things to offer for a low price.
First of all the graphics are not 2016 std. and look a bit old, though it do not matter that much since where are here to drive a bus right ? ;-)
Well the city itself is create well and there is a mix of both ordinary recidential and more dence areas with sky scrapers and conventions centers, and that make it interesting to driver from a-z.
The streets are filled with cars and pedestrians and sometimes even emergency vehicles that you need to let pass.
It also happen that cars drive out in front of you or pedestrians almost walk on the street in front of you, so you need to keep your eyes open. Well I like these small events now and then it make the game interesting.
One other things that make the game interesting is the ability to exit your seat and walk arround in the world and solve small problems. For example a drunk guy enters the bus so you have to get up and ask him to leave.

Anyway you can also invite your friends to come and drive a trip in your bus and follow one of your routes that you create and it is kind of nice i think.
It is also possible to paint your car and stick commercials on it to earn a little more, though It not really where that important to me.

However the controls of the game are not that facinating.
First of all the game do not yet support Trackir ( the dev. wrote on the forum that they consider implementing it ).
So many people are now forced to use the mouse to look arround or setup X and Y key on their wheel to look left and right. No matter what it is not the same as trackir and free look with the mouse. ALso I really miss the ability to look 90 degrees left and right in the bus since it is hard to see the trafic when at a T crossing and only can look 75-80 degrees left and right.
Well all in all I think price level is good fair price for the product. The game is not bad, and have many nice features ( like you can hear small talk in the bus, such as boss i cant go to work today ).

At first glance I had a lot of assumptions about what this game would be, not anything to do with story or characters, but the type of genre the game inhabits and how it goes about that. In many ways it met those assumptions and while I was right it still managed to exceed my thoughts.
A few screens and videos and to me this came off as a simplified metroid-like with a more straight forward beat-em up presentation. And my deep abiding love for any exploration based game was left mildly wanting to know that it really has more in line with Odin Sphere/Muramasa than Metroid it still has enough exploratory quirks to ever so slightly scratch that itch.
What brings this simplicity bright, to me, is the trappings that are around the basic structure. The combat is fine to me, I don't find it completely compelling but it is satisfying in the way your character feels powerful and the agency through which you give him that power is what compels me through the game. Items, leveling up, quests. The depth is not great but it's all deep enough to just make the rest of it so easy to breeze through and feel constantly in a state of needing to get more from the game because it has the ability to give you more. I feel this lust for progress on the mechanical/statistical spectrum that drives me through the game itself elegantly.
And that's not to say the story is creating any sort of roadblock to that. It's actually very well put together and while nearly cloying and childish at times it has an aspect that reflects back this younger version of yourself. Old Saturday morning cartoons, Disney movies, or even just any broadly aimed animated feature. It plays into that in a way that almost makes it okay to be so silly or ardent in child-like way. It's also interesting in how juxtaposed that is to the darker aspects of the story and how easily it accomplishes that without feeling overbearing or too self-serious. And it's startling how good the voice acting is in this game, disregarding some odd lines that sound re-recorded and not quite on point as the same voice from the same session.
The gameplay itself may not be memorable to me but it really is fun to play and progress through. It may feel a little simplistic to start or jarringly sharp or oppressive in its presentation but I think its just so out of our usual context for that type of over the top character expression that it feels wrong at first, though over time it felt right at home.

- Gameplay becomes very easy once you get the idea on how to handle those punching bags called "monsters"
- Balance is managed by sheer damage. Should've added more divercity to the endgame boss battles and enemy attacks
--------------------------------
Tips for beginners:
- Play on hardcore. You will have some problems at the beginning, but don't be afraid to experiment.
- Learn how to counter attack. It will take some time to learn the timing, especially with the first tree miniboss and those mothafrakking slimes...
- Don't sell red crystals. Since monsters respawn after each load, it could save a lot of time for you. Also usefull for learning the monster patterns, without having to reload too often
- Don't save money. Towards the end you will have over 100k unused gold.
- You can't reach some areas. You should come back once you get the required skills
- Max level is 60. You will be able to max all skills. Though Fidget is by far the best one.
- Fidget is your friend. She will tell you (a popup when enter the area) if there is a missed secret on the map
- Unlock "friends" from the cages. There are 12 of them and it will give you wooping 60% health bonus total.
- Don't rush the game and play only few hours at a time. You will finish it in 15-30 hours.
--------------------------------
Overall a great Metroidvania kind of game that's easily worth its full price. It could use a little bit more TLC and depth to the gameplay mechanics and NPC's.

I can't say enough about Hotline Miami. I must admit that I am a retro game lover, and I am one of the people who will never grow tired of the indie flood of 8 and 16 bit games. Hotline Miami looks retro, but that is where that ends. I lived through the 8 bit and 16 bit era and we never got anything like this. The controls are so smooth that even if you are not familiar with the format, if you play any games, you will have a blast with this one. There is the forgiving nature of infinite continues, and if you are just playing it through, not set on getting an A+ for every scene, you can work out a strategy for every level. There are some levels that just picking the right mask is all of the strategy you need, but there are a million ways to beat each and every level.
I can't get over the soundtrack. It almost hypnotizes you into rhis land of senseless repetitive violence, and it makes the game that much more enjoyable. I was a huge fan of Nicholas Winding Refn's movie Drive,  and though the violence is turned up a million othces, I can definitely see the movie's influence on the game in the Jacket scenes. It also has the draw of being something you can just pick up and play whenever you are having a bad day just to blow off some steam by crushing some bad guy skulls in and watching them spray around the room.
Is it worth $9.99? Absolutely. Luckily, with it being an older game you can wait and find it on sale as well. But the beauty of it being an older game made with retro graphics, it is essentially ageless. You go into the game knowing that the pixel graphics are on purpose, and I cannot foresee the ease of control ever being improved upon. I will always be down to reccomend this game to anyone (except maybe easily impressionable youths). If you don't have it, get it. If you have it but never sat down and invested time in it to get the hang of it, play it. Play it until you reach the end. Then come back here and give this awesome game the credit it deserves for being the most amazing game ever made by such a small group of people.

If murder simulation is a genre, Hotline Miami is its new exemplar.
The top-down action game coerces its players to take life in the quickest, ugliest and most ironic ways. It's caustic. It's filthy. It's one of the best arguments against casual violence in video games.
All of Hotline Miami's bloodshed is bound in a pulpy crime story. A gang of animal mask-wearing criminals forces a street punk to become their assassin. They leave thinly veiled assassination assignments on his answering machine, sending him onto the streets of 1989 Miami.
This isn't the story of a cold-blooded murderer. Guilt manifests itself mentally and physically. The world of Hotline Miami is dark as squid ink, and bolstered by a crunchy synth soundtrack and wavy neon graphics that combine to form an OK substitute for a bad LSD trip.
The set dressing of the man's apartment is a particularly deft touch. The accumulation of trash and unexpected house guests establishes Hotline Miami's story more succinctly than would cutscenes or lengthy patches of dialogue. As his life goes, so goes his apartment.
Killing — aggressive and violent — is the core of the game. The player can murder with a number of weapons, ranging from the traditional (pistols, machine guns) to the improvised (a pan full of boiling water). Points are rewarded and multiplied by stringing together assassinations and mixing up weapons. Earning the most points requires the player to do the most awful things, turning a high score into a symbol of how depravedly its players behave.
Masks like those worn by your captors can be found or earned. Each grants a special ability — the owl mask makes hidden objects easier to find, for example, and the unicorn mask silences weapons. They are replay tools, most of which changed the way I approached a challenge. I found myself replaying missions to see how they handled with a certain buff or bonus weapon.
Slamming a door into an unsuspecting enemy will stun them. You may then use the dazed goon as a hostage / living shield, the closest the game comes to a defensive maneuver. Defense rarely works. The "hero" is as vulnerable as his enemies, succumbing to a single strike.
And so Hotline Miami is a mix of trial-and-error with run-and-gun. Test a strategy, die and apply what you learned. Never stop moving. You never feel safe; it turns you into a neurotic, mouse-smashing maniac. The second I died, I was hungry to start again. The repetition doesn't feel like a chore because of the quick retry system. Killing in Hotline Miami is more like a sport.'
Murder is messy; you leave behind maimed corpses and Pollock-esque spatterings of blood. Bodies never disappear, a visual decision the developer underlines, bolds and highlights by making players hike through their destruction at the end of each stage.
Playing Hotline Miami made me feel like an empowered homicidal maniac. I punched open the front door, knocked down the first guard, stole his knife and threw it into his colleague's neck. Before the second wave of guards could step out of the patrol room, I'd sliced them in half with a samurai sword stored in the maintenance closet. I ran into a bathroom, grabbed a man from the urinal mid-stream and tossed him to the floor, printing his face in the decorative tiles. Three guards approached the room, but they didn't know I'd trained a shotgun on the doorknob, just waiting for them to enter. And when they did...
Non-violent encounters bookend missions in the world we know: The main character tries to go about his life — renting videos, visiting bars, grabbing pizza — but the dissonance is disorienting for the player and the character. It's refreshing to have a protagonist react believably to the absurdity and tragedy of his behavior.
As the game approached its climax, I found myself asking, Why? Why is the world so inescapably violent and angry?
Hotline Miami admirably does its best to provide an answer. You'll find it buried deep beneath the game's surface â figuratively and literally. It has more to say about our fascination with violence in games than the lion's share of its competition. That the killing is fun made me feel all the worse. Which was the point. Hotline Miami is exceptional not because it's violent, but because it's violent for a reason.
All in all, Hotline Miami is, hands down, my favorite game i've played. I can't reccomend it enough to you.

I have put in over 456.9 hours into this game at the time of this review.  I have played it from the begining, and for some reason I keep coming back to playing this game.  I love the FPS + RTS Commander hybrid nature of the game.  It adds a different element that you just don't have in cames like CS or typical FPS titles.
Pros:
-Graphics hold up for a game 6 years old
-Dedicated player run servers that make it easy to play
-Most services support 20 or 24 players at a time
-Both sides play completely different
-The Dev team still supports this game and continue to add free updates/balance changes
-The game is pretty balanced right now
-Love the replayability
-Even after 400+ hours I still am trying to get better.
Cons:
-Not a ton of players, on average about 130-200 are playing at a time
-Not an easy game to learn.  There are new tutorials, which help.  But this game takes a lot of effort.
-The game centers around resource nodes, and if either side claims an early win on these, then the game is over.  The key is to hold these resource nodes at all cost and protect critical lanes.  This means that the games can often be one sided and frustrating.
-An inexperienced commander can really screw up a game.
-Sometimes teamwork doesn't work well, when you can't communicate and work together you loose.
-No new units, weapons, evolutions to make the game more interesting.

TL:DR Deponia is a pretty good point and click game with some great characters and humour. A few of its puzzles can be a bit frustrating though
Full Version:
The Complete Journey collects together the first three Deponia games into one package with bonus features like Dev commentary and a quest log for example. Deponia is a pretty standard point and click game with a zany off the wall and occasionally dark humour.
The main character Rufus is a massive loser who creates chaos and destruction wherever he goes. However his ego is so overinflated he still thinks he's a great guy.That sounds like an awful choice for a main character but I found Rufus to be quit likeable despite his flaws and he's a great character. The rest of Deponias cast of characters are all wild and wacky enough to make the game entertaining.
As I said above the gameplay is the standard point and click variety. Pick up items and either combine or use them on other stuff to progress through the game, with the occasional mini game popping up.
Good points:
- the complete version collects the first 3 games together with bonus features as icing on the cake. So you get more bang for you buck than you would by buying the games seperately
- Rufus despite being an awful person becomes quite a likeable and entertaining protaganist. The rest of the games cast features loads of strange and entertaining characters as well that add to the games charm
- I like the fact that this game is more aimed at adults with a more crude and dark humour than your typical point and click game.
Bad points:
- a few of the games puzzles are quite frustrating and at times very obtuse or over complicated. For example, without spoiling anything, there was a puzzle that you could only solve by going into the settings and turning off the music. The game only gives you a very vague hint about this and while I'm sure the Devs thought it was a clever and unique solution it felt so out of the box that it was a bit of a pisstake. Fortunately most of the puzzles arent too bad and can be solved with enough investigation or exploring.

Mafia 3 is a wonderful storytelling experience that steeps the player into the culture of the 1960s and 1970s.  From start to finish the story remains engaging and complelling with event beats that create a wonderful pace based on the player's own behavior as they proceed through quests and story events. Every character that you meet going through this world is as interesting and diverse as the setting. So much I believe that the supporting character of Jack Donovan was a scene stealer with every interaction that the story brought him into. And for those interested in how Mafia 2's story plays out for its own protagonist will find some great answers here.
The biggest help for this immersion is the music of the era. Everywhere you go there are radios, jukeboxes, and even car radios that can be listened to that provide music from known artists from that era. One moment you could be mixing it up with Creedence Clearwater's Bad Moon Rising then kicking a station over to Aretha Franklin's Rrespect. All interweaved with talk radio and advertisements representative of the game's local color.
The gameplay for Mafia 3 is similar to other entries into the franchise, in that it too fits the semi-open world over the shoulder third person view of other games like Grand Theft Auto and Assassin's Creed. This can make gun combat difficult at times since a lot of the game uses a cover/stealth mechanic and the use of pseudo-aim down the barrel method that can make lining up shots difficult. Otherwise this means combat is succinct and brutal on the hard settings for those who love a good challenge.
Graphically the game shows its age as it seems to rely upon the same technology used to make Mafia 2. The cutscenes were detailed but in some cases were overshadowed by the lack of good texturing or just bad resolution. And this came through in many of the game models out in the world. can I recommend this Bus simulator, well YES and NO.
And let me start by saying that if you consider buying this or some other bus simulator then I would highly recommend you to buy bus and cable car simulator instead..
Well let me review Bus simulator 16 first, it is actual quite good and have allot of good things to offer for a low price.
First of all the graphics are not 2016 std. and look a bit old, though it do not matter that much since where are here to drive a bus right ? ;-)
Well the city itself is create well and there is a mix of both ordinary recidential and more dence areas with sky scrapers and conventions centers, and that make it interesting to driver from a-z.
The streets are filled with cars and pedestrians and sometimes even emergency vehicles that you need to let pass.
It also happen that cars drive out in front of you or pedestrians almost walk on the street in front of you, so you need to keep your eyes open. Well I like these small events now and then it make the game interesting.
One other things that make the game interesting is the ability to exit your seat and walk arround in the world and solve small problems. For example a drunk guy enters the bus so you have to get up and ask him to leave.
And one in a while you also have to help handicapped people in/out of the bus by exit the bus and extending the ramp ;-)
The all new "run a bus business" feature is nice, and you can even compare how well you are doing to other players though some have kind of unrealistic billion usd scores.
Anyway you can also invite your friends to come and drive a trip in your bus and follow one of your routes that you create and it is kind of nice i think.
It is also possible to paint your car and stick commercials on it to earn a little more, though It not really where that important to me.
Well the bus driving experience is kind of okay. The feeling of sitting in the seat and driving I would say is realistic and the bus feel big ect. And you can also press various keys and sell tickets ect.
The bus is also well made and in general give a good impression.
However the controls of the game are not that facinating.
First of all the game do not yet support Trackir ( the dev. wrote on the forum that they consider implementing it ).
So many people are now forced to use the mouse to look arround or setup X and Y key on their wheel to look left and right. No matter what it is not the same as trackir and free look with the mouse. ALso I really miss the ability to look 90 degrees left and right in the bus since it is hard to see the trafic when at a T crossing and only can look 75-80 degrees left and right.
Well all in all I think price level is good fair price for the product. The game is not bad, and have many nice features ( like you can hear small talk in the bus, such as boss i cant go to work today ).
Also the get in and get out of the bus by passengers work pretty good, and you often fill your bus pretty good with passengers.
I also like that sometimes there are events such as holliday where there are tons of passengers waiting for a ride.
The game it self work in such a way you unlock features by driving from a-b.. in about 3 hour of gameplay I am level 10-11 and have unlocked the biggest bus in the game and half of the map.
To unlock more I need to play the game and get xp, but I can also solve some goals ( such as having 2 bus stops in each unlocked zone ect ).
All in all not a bad game but it do feel a bit like an arcade bus simulator, so I really prefer the older game named "Bus and cablecar simulator" since the busses are a little more realistisc, and the game experience is just a bit more fun and realistic.

This is a very engaging and interesting game. You do more than just drive a bus - you also have to manage your own bus company, organise routes, deal with a variety of interesting situations (bus malfunctions, demanding passengers etc.), buy new buses, hire new drivers and so on. You get missions that help you unlock new features. You're never short of something to do.
Bus Simulator 16 is made by the same people who developed Bus Simulator 2012, albeit with a different partner this time. I gave Bus Simulator 2012 a negative review, but I am happy to say that Bus Simulator 16 is a vast improvement - with one exception. Bus Simulator 2012 had awful frame rates, and unfortunately, so does Bus Simulator 2016 at present. I played on medium graphic settings with a pretty powerful computer, but found the gameplay very laggy and choppy, although just bearable. But I can play games like Euro Truck Simulator 2 or Train Simulator 2016 on high settings and have no FPS issues. So this is an area that needs work. And apparently, the developers are working on it, so hopefully performance will be much better soon.
Some areas where Bus Simulator 2016 has improved on BS 2012 include keyboard steering (much, MUCH better, more like Euro Truck or American Truck Simulator steering now), AI traffic (much more sensible, accidents are usually due to your bad driving rather than their stupidity) and user-friendliness of the bus interior (no more password to enter, selling tickets is now much more efficiently handled). And of course, it introduces new things that were never seen in BS 2012, like the whole company management deal, missions and so on.
Other than the need for performance optimisation, I have few complaints about this game. It is definitely the best bus simulator since OMSI 2, and has real potential to give the latter a serious run for its money. I am more than happy to recommend it.

Overview:
The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings is a fantasy RPG set in a medieval landscape.  The player controls Geralt of Rivia as he trys to uncover the truth behind the events that take place in the beginning of the game.  An expansive story awaits and is effected by the player's actions.  The choices you make really will effect the outcome of events.
Pros:
A great and detailed story.  The story is definitely the best aspect of this game.  There are a lot of important characters throughout the game who will shape events as they unfold.
Content.  There is a lot of content here.  Each area has a few side quests in addition to the main story quests.  Even if you just stick to the main quests, the story will take you around 30 hours.  Crafting is also available and can take a considerable amount of time.  If you want a break from the main game, an arena area is available with leaderboards.
Cons:
Crafting.  Don't bother trying to craft that really awesome armor set the vendor is selling.  For one, you will probably never get the money to even buy all the recipes.  If you do manage that, it can be quite time consuming to gather all the leather.  Each armor set comes with a sword recipe for your regular and silver sword.  The swords are the worst part of this crafted set.  They are really awesome for the current area, but require you to have the complete set equiped to use.  Each time you move to a new area in the game, the previous armor set recipes become unavailable.  So, if you spent time just crafting the swords and move to the next area, all that time and resources are now gone.  Crafting armor pieces can be pointless as better or equivalent items can be found by simply thoroughly exploring the area or gambling with random NPCs.  Other than potions and enhancements, crafting is just a waste of time.
Combat.  Although Geralt has access to a few spells in addition to swords, the combat is rather simple.  You can easily play the entire game just slashing as fast as you can and dodging away.  You can parry your opponent by waiting for them to attack, but this locks your character in place and is not advisable when taking on multiple opponents.  Since basically every fight has you facing multiple opponents, parrying can leave you open.
Story Presentation.  The story is pretty good, but sometimes it is not presented very well.  The player mainly controls Geralt but at times will very briefly control a side character.  This can happen at random times and can be better handled by just showing a cut scene.
Tech Issues.  The audio in the game is all over the place.  Sometimes character dialog will be very loud and other times a wisper.  I also did not care for the narrator's voice when transitioning to new areas.  When I had a lot of saves the game would continually crash when trying to load.
Level Design.  The world consist of mainly tight corridors with very little open space.  It would have been nice to have more room to roam around.
Conclusion:
The Witcher 2 presents a great story in a not so great way.  The levels feel claustrophobic, the combat can be very simple, and the crafting can be pointless.  If you put that aside, this is still a pretty good game.  There is a deep story here that can be guided by the player.  If you haven't played a serious RPG in awhile and are looking for something decent, play this.

Final Fantasy VII is one of those games that everyone knows. It was revolutionary when it first came out for the PS1, and was one of the best selling games of 1997. The PC port is amazing. The original soundtrack was replaced with a newer soundtrack, and the graphics were also dramatically improved. I, personally, did not enjoy the music that was put into the PC port of this. However, with the aid of mods, I was able to replace the PC soundtrack with the classic PS1 soundtrack.  The PC port also offers 3 different graphics choices, depending on the preferences of the user. The user can choose between the PS1 graphics, or the PC graphics, as well as a mod that gives combat 3D graphics. One downside of this game, is the fact that you have to create a Square Enix account to play. This was a disappointment for me, but not enough to keep me from playing it. Aside from the technical aspects of this game, the gameplay is amazing. This is by far, the best game I have ever owned, because of the great story, the great soundtrack, the amazing combat, and the replayability. After spending over 500 hours on this game over three different game systems, I won't be stopping any time soon. I highly recommend FFVII, and honestly, this game is worth much more than $11.99.

TL:DR Deponia is a pretty good point and click game with some great characters and humour. A few of its puzzles can be a bit frustrating though
Full Version:
The Complete Journey collects together the first three Deponia games into one package with bonus features like Dev commentary and a quest log for example. Deponia is a pretty standard point and click game with a zany off the wall and occasionally dark humour.
The main character Rufus is a massive loser who creates chaos and destruction wherever he goes. However his ego is so overinflated he still thinks he's a great guy.That sounds like an awful choice for a main character but I found Rufus to be quit likeable despite his flaws and he's a great character. The rest of Deponias cast of characters are all wild and wacky enough to make the game entertaining.
As I said above the gameplay is the standard point and click variety. Pick up items and either combine or use them on other stuff to progress through the game, with the occasional mini game popping up.
Good points:
- the complete version collects the first 3 games together with bonus features as icing on the cake. So you get more bang for you buck than you would by buying the games seperately
- Rufus despite being an awful person becomes quite a likeable and entertaining protaganist. The rest of the games cast features loads of strange and entertaining characters as well that add to the games charm
- I like the fact that this game is more aimed at adults with a more crude and dark humour than your typical point and click game.
Bad points:
- a few of the games puzzles are quite frustrating and at times very obtuse or over complicated. For example, without spoiling anything, there was a puzzle that you could only solve by going into the settings and turning off the music. The game only gives you a very vague hint about this and while I'm sure the Devs thought it was a clever and unique solution it felt so out of the box that it was a bit of a pisstake. Fortunately most of the puzzles arent too bad and can be solved with enough investigation or exploring.

Mafia 3 is a wonderful storytelling experience that steeps the player into the culture of the 1960s and 1970s.  From start to finish the story remains engaging and complelling with event beats that create a wonderful pace based on the player's own behavior as they proceed through quests and story events. Every character that you meet going through this world is as interesting and diverse as the setting. So much I believe that the supporting character of Jack Donovan was a scene stealer with every interaction that the story brought him into. And for those interested in how Mafia 2's story plays out for its own protagonist will find some great answers here.
The biggest help for this immersion is the music of the era. Everywhere you go there are radios, jukeboxes, and even car radios that can be listened to that provide music from known artists from that era. One moment you could be mixing it up with Creedence Clearwater's Bad Moon Rising then kicking a station over to Aretha Franklin's Rrespect. All interweaved with talk radio and advertisements representative of the game's local color.
The gameplay for Mafia 3 is similar to other entries into the franchise, in that it too fits the semi-open world over the shoulder third person view of other games like Grand Theft Auto and Assassin's Creed. This can make gun combat difficult at times since a lot of the game uses a cover/stealth mechanic and the use of pseudo-aim down the barrel method that can make lining up shots difficult. Otherwise this means combat is succinct and brutal on the hard settings for those who love a good challenge.
Graphically the game shows its age as it seems to rely upon the same technology used to make Mafia 2. The cutscenes were detailed but in some cases were overshadowed by the lack of good texturing or just bad resolution. And this came through in many of the game models out in the world. There also seemed to be a few persistent bugs that required a full reboot of the game - such as the furniture in diners being relocated completely outside the store as if the models were incorrectly placed, or the minimap and ability to interface with objects and people disappearing. This could become quite frustrating when trying to complete mission objectives or interact with vital NPCs to forward the story along.
In the end I recommend Mafia 3 for the great soundtrack and storytelling experience. Fans of Mafia 2 will enjoy Mafia 3 because it continues the quality they've come to expect and new entries will be introduced to the best story in the franchise so far.

First thing one should know before playing this game: At the start the main protagonist will come off as a total♥♥♥♥♥♥ A real self centered, egotistical ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, whose antics would make an SJW's balls recede into its body and come out the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. But that's what makes him likeable and unique from other cookie-cut 'good' main characters. And your opinion of him will most likely get better anyway as his character develops, which is par for the course as the story progresses.
Second: Like most point and click adventure games, the nature of its interaction mechanics and stuff crafting will present you with problems whose solutions follow some dumb frustrating logic. There were many times where I got stuck on a screen because I didn't point this one specific thing to this other specific inconspicuous thing that no one would think would go together in the first place.
So Third: Save yourself some time and go look at a walkthrough once you see that no option you'd thought of would progress the game. If you thought that you've exhausted all possible combinations of all the crap in your inventory and environment, there's no point in being stubborn and keep clicking the same things over and over when the solution's something minor you probably simply overlooked. Sure you would have found it eventually, but you would have also wasted your time.
Lastly: Don't take it too seriously, and enjoy! Every character is quirky, the world is interesting, and it's got a ton of fun minigames. It's got a lot of really funny ridiculous moments, and some really dark moments and mature themes too. So it's a real rollercoaster ride, and gets a solid thumbs up from me.

At this moment i been playing the game for 3 hours. The first impressions are nice. You take over the bus company from a old man who is gonna retire. Up to you to build out the company and keep it healthy while you drive around in busses yourself as well.
I really like how they put in little details with the passengers. In other bus simulators they are rather static and only react to certain things when you mess up. In Bus Simulator 16 your passengers talk with others so you can hear the conversations at times, they play around with their phone, checking for messages or playing games on it. But not for the whole ride, its not a animation that keeps playing till they leave the bus.
Pedestrians also feel more alive, when they cross a street and a car is getting close they start to run.
Emergency vehicles now also make their way trough the traffic, passing by when someone is standing still. A huge improvement over the others where they tend to stay behind cars and waiting in line till its their turn. They also drive trough the red light so you have make sure you let them go first when you hear the sirens.
Another great thing are random events like maintenance to the road that makes you have to take a detour, problems with the bus you need to fix and you even get passengers in wheelchairs that you actually have to help with the ramp depending on what bus you are controlling. Don't forget this cause me and others already didn't notice them and drove off just to get the message i forgot a passenger.
There are also some minor things. If you are a die hard simmer then this game might be a bit to arcady for you. Unlike it's competition you don't need to remember a lot of buttons and manage all aspects of the bus to make sure the temperature and such is good enough.
This makes it easyer for beginners to get into or those who like driving a bus but find the competition to hard, but for those who are looking for the next big bus simulator this might be a disapointment.
There are also some optimization issues going on, when you read the negative reviews you will see a few of them. I personally haven't had the game crash on me once, nor having any bug showing up ingame. Though the game could use some optimzation, i first thought it was my pc but reading the negative reviews it is the game appearantly. Though i lower my range of view and that helped alot with the fps drops.
There are also long loading screens, however once it loaded the city it has loaded everything so when you unlocked the city you can drive around without any issues.
There is also a multiplayer aspect though that means you can get a friend drive routes for your company and earn money for your company. Sadly you can't see them driving around in the same world. I hope they will add this cause that would be great.
The good:
+ Create your own routes
+ Passengers feel more alive then before
+ Nice details in behavior from emergency vehicles, pedestrians and passengers
+ Random events
The minor:
- Perhaps to arcady for the die hard simmers
- Could use a bit more optimization (though it isn't to bad)
- No other players in your world when playing the multiplayer

The Basement Collection is an interesting bundle of games, to say the least.
The Basement Collection is a series of flash games that Edmund McMillan created before he made Super Meat Boy and The Binding of Issac. These include Meat Boy, Time ♥♥♥♥, Spewer, Aether, Triachnid, Coil, and Grey Matter.
While not all of these games are fully polished, each is unique in its own way. Time ♥♥♥♥ has you trapped in a box switching dimensions, Aether involves a boy exploring space on the back of a monster, and Spewer is exactly what you think it is.
While these were all free games originally, they all have been refined in some way, either with new content, redone graphics, or refined controls. They also come with hours worth of unlockables and bonus content that ranges from development sketches, interviews, game soundtracks, old comics, and more.
Do be warned that these games are coded in flash, so you might experience slow down for some of these games, even if you have a decent computer. However, this is a minor complaint.
You might not like everything in this bundle, but with the raw amount of content on offer, and the measly low asking price, this package is defiantly worth a look for those curious. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for something fun and a little bit different than the norm. Just be warned that once you dive into the Basement Collection, you just might never want to come back out again.

It's apparent that stillalive studios has made a wholeheartedly attempt at making a bus simulator.
The game lets you control everything from opening the garage door to printing tickets and giving change to you customers. The games UI feels fresh and modern and is pretty easily navigated. I like that you can make your own bus routes and assign drivers to drive them.
Unfortunately for me, the games falls flat in one of the most important mechanics, the driving part.
The handling feels very loose and the bus veers all over the place, and I'm playing on a controller with the sensitivity on its minimum setting. It doesn't feel like you are steering a 14-ton bus when it jerks at the smallest input on the joystick.
As mentioned by other players, the voice acting is not very good. At all. And before reaching my first hour of playtime i was already hearing the same chatter from the people in my bus as i was hearing in the beginning, it seems that they haven't recorded that many lines for people to say.
The game has a couple of pretty interesting mechanics though. The doors on the bus can jam and you will be forced to close them manually, emergency vehicles can rush up behind you with their sirens on wanting you to move over, there's dynamical construction sites and more stuff.
But ultimately, for me, the game has potential but i cannot recommend it in its current state. The steering is too off and the game has some obvious optimization issues. I'm considering refunding it and maybe coming back if it's patched.

tl;dr Reminiscent of Dishonored, I would definitely recommend picking this game up during the next sale if you are a fan of stealth games with super powers.
If you are a fan of Dishonored, and you are a fan of stealth games, this game is worth checking out.  Much like Dishonored, Aragami is a stealth game where you sneak around killing guards while you slowly unlock your full arsenal of special abilities.  The mechanics of this game are solid, you can easily and quickly teleport from one guard to the next, chaining together your stealth assassination while feeling like a total badass.
Where this game really lacks is in it’s variety and story.  Unlike many other stealth games, there is nothing to do in Aragami besides sneak around and stab dudes.  There are a couple scrolls per level that will give you skill points that you can use to unlock your abilities, but besides those, there is no loot, no secrets, and no lore for you to stumble across while you’re playing.  Additionally, the levels in Aragami get very repetitive very quickly, and the are only two types of enemies you encounter throughout the game.
With that being said, Aragami is an indie title and it comes at an indie price.  Aragami is a solid game, one that I love to hop into and play a quick level every so often.  The mechanics are great and I think the couple of boss fights throughout the game are an interesting twist on the traditional stealth genre.  While the repetitive nature keeps me from recommending this game at full price, I definitely recommend picking this game up during the next sale.  If you are a fan of stealth games, super powers, and feelings likely a total badass, this is a game worth checking out.

Dust: An Elysian Tail is an fantastic game. Beautiful hand-drawn art, visuals and animations, fantastic soundtrack and voice acting, as well as characters and story. Combat is fluid with every button press and sword swing.
Your main character, Dust, is an energetic, humorous furry warrior who (like in many games) lost his memory and goes on a quest to find out who he actually is. On this quest he is acompanied by Blade of Ahrah (a talking blade, yes) and Blades diminutive guardian Fidget which makes for a lot of fun throughout the game. Story is beautifuly written and both main and side quests offer you hours and hours of playing without getting bored. Combat style is as many would say is "easy-to-learn, difficult-to-master" type with usually dozens of enemies on the screen and with many possibilities and tricks makes for a very good combat system.
There are some cons here and there like enemies and bosses being very easy early in game (but they get a lot harder in later parts of game and make for formidable opponents), some items being overly expensive early on and as much as Dust have nice moves and attacks, few more combos or attacks would always be nice.
All in all, Dust: An Elysian Tail is everything you could want in an action rpg, and it is one of my most favorite games of all time.
I would highly recommend this game not only to RPG fans, but to all gamers out there to atleast give it a try.
