DEFCON, in simple terms, is a simulator/game where you can destroy entire countries and continents by using nuclear weapons to decimate populations and cities whilst watching them burn. You can choose to be either North America (Canada, USA), South America (All South American countries), Africa (All African countries), Asia (Most Asian countries and far east countries), Europe (All European countries) or just Russia (Just russia, duh). There is a DEFCON timer, in which it starts from DEFCON 5 all the way to DEFCON 1, signalling nuclear war. The DEFCON system is a US defence and readiness condition system in which state the military should be readied at, depending on the current condition, five to one. Slowly or very quickly depending on what speed you want it on, the DEFCON level will drop until it reaches DEFCON 1 and nuclear war will begin. The game is based on a film called Wargames (1983) and is about a hacker who gains control of NORAD's nuclear missiles and threatens nuclear war. The GUI and game is very similar to Wargames' control systems and computer simulations. In order to start the game you need to select one of the continents, you can place down radars, missile silos and airbases. Each one of these has a certain strategic importance. Radars can detect incoming nuclear missiles from nuclear submarines or land based silos and show their trajectories. Airbases have the ability to launch fighter and bombers to city targets or fleets of ships in the oceans, the bombers can also drop one nuke onto a city or military target. Silos obviously have the ability to fire up to 10 missiles anywhere at a target. Silos can also become air defence systems in which they will shoot down incoming missiles, fighters and bombers within their range. There is also the ability to place fleets of ships (nuclear missile equipped submarines, battleships and aircraft carriers). Submarines can attack ships on the surface of the sea and sink them and can also fire nukes at cities within a shorter range than silos but they are more stealthy. Battleships are an all-round ship, they can attack all kinds of ships including aircraft. Aircraft carriers can launch nuke bombers to cities or military targets and attack them and launch fighter jets to attack ships. It is also worth mentioning, you can't win. It is impossible to win. As the games motto/slogan says "Everybody Dies". The whole object is to loose the 'least' by having less casualties. For each 1 million citizens killed, your continent gains 2 points, for every 1 million citizens killed on your continent, you loose 1 point. The game is easy to grasp but can be a bit challenging at times and difficult to use. It does take time to learn, but hey, its really cheap on sales and what isn't good about nuking the ♥♥♥♥ out of Africa?

Generally I only play shooters but in the games that give you the option to, I find myself playing quite stealthily. I also remember Tenchu from PS1 and found myself looking for a game with a similar kind of experience, this is when I stumbled across 'Aragami'. I read some reviews and one mentioned it's similarities to Tenchu, I immediately added it to my wishlist and bought it a few days later during a sale on a 3rd party gaming website.
Some games take a while to get into and get me hooked but 'Aragami' was different, it was an instant hit for me. I loved the simplicity of the controls and the easy learning curve early in the game that made sure I would look forward to the next challenge. There are multiple ways to succeed in each level, go completely stealth or trick and confuse your enemies with an option to sneak past or take them out. Whichever method I used I never got frustrated or wanted to stop playing until I finished a level.
Graphics are nice too, kind of cartoony style which reminded me of games like Borderlands 2 and The Walking Dead.
The only real downsides for me are the length of the game and the achievements. I completed the game in about 12-15 hours of play and got most achievements quite easily, some requiring a few attempts. The only replay value I feel 'Aragami' has is to go for the 100% as you can't get this on 1 playthrough. Also, there is a level editor which is something I like to dabble in sometimes, however, I've not tried it yet so can't really comment but making or playing community levels may go towards extending the overall experience for some.
The game also advertises multiplayer and co-op but as far as I've seen only co-op exists, there's no real MP available. To be honest I'm not sure how this game would work in MP but if the developers could figure it out it could be quite interesting and would be very different from your normal MP experience.

The biggest problem of Natural Selection has always been that even in the most casual of matchups, there is a heavy reliance on teamwork. There's no way to Rambo in a game like this, which means you're only as strong as the people you're working with. It's great as a high-level competitive e-sport, but for people who just want something to play in their free time, this isn't the right game. If you're a newbie you're going to get chewed out constantly by people who *know* what they're doing and are really vocal about how bad you are to the entire team (since it isn't just a matter of K/D ratio, you need to coordinate resource captures, base strikes, base defense, buliding, etc. etc.), or you're going to be the guy that knows what he's doing, and feel like a loser for getting frustrated that people who don't play as much as you are ruining a *video game* for you.
Aside from that, the load times are still ridiculously long, and the game has ludicrously high system requirements, either because it isn't well optimized or it's too big for its own good (the longer games go on, the more tech both sides have which means more effects going off at once, and there's also more buildings, more creep for the game to render).
It's a really great concept, but the realization is that a game like this is too massive to be wielded. The engine collapses upon itself regularly, and you aren't going to even be an "average" player without being able to play this game like a full-time job.
The 6 is not because it's a bad game, it's just too ambitious for its own good. I feel like the development team is composed of a bunch of hardcore gamers that are passionate about their work and wanted to take a genius idea they had and share it with the world, but they didn't have anyone around to rein them in and keep them in reality. In NS1 or NS2. Which is a real shame, because if this game was even half of what it is right now, it'd not only remain as a unique multiplayer FPS in a sea of derivative titles, it'd likely actually be a better game all around.

This is a revised review to go along with the massive 1.6 game rework update.
Originally, my negative score for the game was based on 2 things:
1. The moba/pvp aspect of the game was mediocre and dull, and was out shined by pretty much all other moba style games
2. The PvE tower defense aspect of the game had been drastically neutered and watered down to the point of being boring and unappealing.
With update 1.6 the first issue was done away with. There is no more moba/pvp aspect to the game. The devs went full circle and decided to take the game back to its roots - PvE Tower Defense. This was a great move on their part. I wish this huge change alone was enough (at the current time) to give the game a glowing thumbs up. Unfortunately, while is a HUGE leap in the right direction, the game still needs a ton of work. I feel its better to leave a thumbs down to help encourage the devs to keep improving the game and its flaws, and give it a thumbs up when they have done this.
So, about #2. I will quote my original beefs with the PvE Tower Defense aspects of the game, and list where they currently stand now:
Here is one complaint from my original review that I feel hasnt much improved at all. Sure, they seem to have tweaked all heroes, making them a bit more "fast paced" for the PvE game mode. You seem to be able to use your abilities more often which is nice, but my main gripes about the heroes still exists:
1. Heroes are way more limited in OMDU than in past OMD games. You are stuck with 1 weapon, and have 2 abilities. There is ZERO customization when it comes to each heroes weapon and powers. No ability to equip things like amulets which grant new powers, or a different weapon for a different style of attacking.
2. Perks gained from leveling up during a match are just plain awful, boring, and most of the time something I dont even care about. Imagine someone saying, "You get to pick between these 3 different ice cream flavors" only... you dont like ice cream AND its feezing outside. So you spend a few moments trying to find the best of the worst to pick from, and go with that. Most of these "upgrade" perks are super boring. They are just too minor of a change to have any real impact on the gameplay, or any impact on how that character plays.
Most of the time I find myself asking, "Why would anyone even WANT an upgrade like that? Its pointless" or "Wow, that ugprade is so insignificantly small, its not worth taking."
The devs need to take a page from blizzards book from Heroes of the Storm (since thats a similar model to what heroes in this game follow), and look at how heroes in that game improve when they get upgrades.  A good tip: Dont do upgrades that just buff powers by a % amount. Instead, buff powers by changing how that power actually works or adding a new mechanic to that power.
Example: If a hero gets a single target stun, offer an upgrade that turns that single target stun, into an AOE slow instead as one of the options.
3. Hero Balance - This wasnt part of my original issue, but it is an issue none the less. Some heroes just feel a lot more gimpy than others. You can see these when a good player still cant get scores anywhere near what other players get with other heroes at the end of a map. This is often due to lack of AoE attacks.
Other times, like with Cyngus, its due to a dumb mechanic. In his case, its making his default hero attack the only one in the game that costs mana. There is nothing special about his attack. It makes zero sense that he must use mana just to use his default attack when no one else does.
Out of all my issues still with the game, Heroes are the one thing I feel devs still need to do LOTS of work on. Especially when it comes to level up perks, and balance between heroes. (skins need a lot of work too - THIS IS HOW YOU WILL MAKE MONEY DEVS!)
This has improved by about 50%. Its mainly a map issue. Along with update 1.6, the devs have released a handful of new maps. All of these maps are great. They allow for much better trap placement and strategy (just like orcs must die 1 and 2). No complaints here at all.
On the other hand, the original OMDunchained maps are still part of the rotation. This maps are just awful. More centered around moba "lane" gameplay. Getting one of these maps on a random game queue always makes me just want to quit out. THEY ARE NO FUN, and should be removed from the game, or completely redesigned following the examples of the newly added PvE maps. Until something like this happens, the original issue I had above is not something I feel is resolved yet.
This has been improved in almost all aspects. Due to not needing to balance traps and progress around competitive play, the assortment of traps and how you unlock them has been greatly improved upon. I'm an expert in Bomberman but I have only tested this game for an half hour to check the game mechanics. Here are my impressions.
TL;DR:
++ Competitive online gameplay with ranking.
-- No controls configuration (for now). The developers don't seem to think this feature is useful since there are only 2 buttons.
My general impression: I recommend this game for couch gaming but this game is not tight enough for competitive Bomberman players so I won't recommend it for competitive.
In details:
Pros:
++ First and most important point: competitive online game play. I have only a bunch of friends who likes Bomberman and among them only 3 who are really good at it. Bringing online game play with competitive rank is the major and most important feature that no other Bomberman did outside Japan. Unfortunately I haven't tested it so I can't say if it's any good but I do believe this is the most important feature for a Bomberman game.
++ There are 2 kind of Bombermans in my opinion: classic ones (Bomberman 93', 94, Mega Bomberman, Saturn Bomberman) and the Super Nintendo ones. This game is clearly a classic one. I personally dislike the SNES-like ones so this is an important point for me.
+ Almost all you need to know is in the doc on their website:
+ Up to 128 players. This is the kind of game that is fun to play with 10 people on the same screen. Very cool feature for local multiplayer but I believe this is not suitable for competitive (2, 4 or 5 players are the good numbers (3 is unbalanced, more than 5 is messy)).
+ The screenshots look bad but I must say the graphics are actually quite nice. Especially the forest style and the classic green background with bricks.
+ Character customization. You can pick one of the 6 skins and select 2 colors of your choice to customize it.
+ King of the hill mode (not tested)
Deal breaker:
- No controls configuration (for now)
I'm not sure what is the intention of the developers exactly because they did add a control configuration menu to the game but apparently it does nothing (at least for the gamepad configuration) and on the website they seems to think it is not useful: "There is no in-game controller configuration, as there are only two main actions ("primary" - drop bomb, and "secondary" for pinging and powerups) and all face buttons should automatically be assigned alternatingly to those two actions."
Their argument sounds okay but in my personal opinion this makes the game unsuitable for competitive game. Imagine any other game you play competitive without being able to adapt the controls. I'm very used to the Saturn Bomberman controls so any other configuration makes me lose a little bit.
Cons:
- No kangaroo/dino ability (no need for a third button)
- Remote control. It uses the same button to detonate it than to stop a bomb in movement. By default the item behave differently: only the next bomb you drop will be remote and then it's like you lose the item. I personally don't see the point of having one remote controlled bomb that you can't choose when you want to start using it. This item seems also useless in the beginning of the game. It also reduces the probability to get one of the other items. The original remote control item is quite unsuitable for multiplayer gameplay (you just kill basically whoever you want). I don't know how it works in competitive, I haven't tested. But if you can customize it then I would say playing a game on different rules on every game is not good for competitive.
- Taunt (a third button). You can taunt the other players during the game. This feature blocks your controls for more than a full second while your character is saying something provocative. This is a completely useless feature that has negative impact on the game play. Fortunately I think I saw a switch to turn it off. I don't know how it works in competitive.
- Not square shaped maps. One of the principle of Bomberman is to have everybody at equal distance. Rectangular maps break this rule. This can be useful for 6-players gameplay though.
- No power glove. No ability to kick bombs over blocks. Screen wrapping is so much fun in Bomberman but here I didn't see trampolines nor power gloves nor blue kangaroos that can kick a bomb at the other side of the screen.
- Choosing the player color. You can pick 2 colors and one of the 6 skins. This is very cool but you have to do it every time you start the game on a menu screen that is actually a map where you're going to move your character. Selecting the character and the number of bot there feels very awkward. I don't know how it works in competitive but you can't configure a default skin so I expect you have to do it at least one time when you start the game but I suspect you have to do it at every game. Also everybody picks their color of their choice so you may end up changing color at every game. This is not good for competitive.
Possible fixes:
- Replace remote control by mines like in Saturn Bomberman in the Jungle stage
- Enforce competitive rules if it's not already the case: pick one rule for everybody, no customization
- Enforce 2, 4 or 5 players in a map at equal distance in competitive
- Add "aura" to characters: enemies in red, allies in blue (= everybody is red except your own character)
- Customize your online skin in the configuration menu so people won't have to select it again
- Add power glove because it doesn't require a third button and it's fun
- Add trampolines
- Remove "open space" in competitive (4 walkable tiles in square). It feels awkward in a Bomberman because the bombs explodes only in the lines of the four directions of a bomb.
- Remove taunts or at least remove the time where the controls are blocked. This feature shouldn't have impact on the game
- If you're not afraid to introduce a third button, add dino's/kangaroo's abilities

This Bomberman style game is already great, and still has massive potential.
I've been playing multiplayer Bomberman games since back in the days of Super Bomberman and Mega Bomberman for the Genesis.  I've been eagerly waiting for a good PC Bomberman game for a very long time, and this one satisfies the craving.
It has many unique features including the unique level variety. There are levels that don't follow the standard grid pattern, have open areas, and other non-typical layouts, as well as sizes ranging from small to huge.  It has rideable creatures like the Louies from Mega Momberman. Not to mention you can set up massive matches with up to 64 players.  Its pure insanity!
Even in its current form, it's well worth the price, but I can't wait to see where it goes after more updates that hopefully add more in depth powerup type and frequency customization, and similar match customization features.  I think this game has the potential to be the best Bomberman style game ever.

Aragmi is, in it's purest form, a true stealth game. Not one for the hack and slash "stealth" games, but a literal silent ninja where everything must be either to decieve, kill without being scene, or even just plain out avoid enemies altogether.
Now, within the stealth game routes, this game amazingly has tons of freedom. You can do any of the afore mentioned tactics, a combination of some, or any other stealth idea you can image. The gameplay feels very intuitive and the shadow arts that you get make you truely feel like a ninja of the shadows; teleporting, sneaking, and transforming the shadows to your will. This is not a game for those who like pure action and beat-'em-up games. But if you're looking for a very high quality stealth game in which you can be in covert missions however you see fit and have the power of practically night its self, this is the best game out there for you. This DEFINITELY should be picked up by any stealth fans, as it does the genre justice and beyond.

Gather round children, I have a story for you.
Once there was a game I liked quite a lot,
Orcs Must Die! Unchained was great fun.
It was closer to a MOBA this time, but not,
Oh how delightful twas to watch the orcs run.
Robot Games seemed on the right track,
adding new characters and content
with each and every update pack
made the games mix of fun more potent.
Then Robot games had an idea
Of how to make cash really quick
they said to anyone who could hear
"that content just wont stick"
But nobody listened,
they were too busy playing
and when the update was christened
it turned to dismaying
For everyones skins, traps and stats
were reset to zero, all gold turned back
but not into cash, no not that,
we might have lost less cash were we hacked
"No refunds past 90 days
The skins are now random drops.
we understand your unwillingess to play
but we're afraid we cannot stop"
And so it was that I told them they were crooks,
for taking my cash AND my content,
they knew which skin i had lost, info not in a book,
so I told them of my intent.
"if you cannot give me my $15 skin
or even just my fifteen dollars
Ill have to put a bad review in
to alert any consumers."
"We're sorry, but those skins just wont stay"
"That's fine," I said, "but i dont support companies that do business that way."
And now youve heard my story today.
Obviously those aren't direct quotes, because if they had rhymed that well I'd have been concerned I was hallucinating. But the basic jist of it remained the same. I bought a skin from them to support their free-to-play game and they took it away from me with the latest update, the level reset didnt even bother me that much, but the skin does. This is a revised review to go along with the massive 1.6 game rework update.
Originally, my negative score for the game was based on 2 things:
1. The moba/pvp aspect of the game was mediocre and dull, and was out shined by pretty much all other moba style games
2. The PvE tower defense aspect of the game had been drastically neutered and watered down to the point of being boring and unappealing.
With update 1.6 the first issue was done away with. There is no more moba/pvp aspect to the game. The devs went full circle and decided to take the game back to its roots - PvE Tower Defense. This was a great move on their part. I wish this huge change alone was enough (at the current time) to give the game a glowing thumbs up. Unfortunately, while is a HUGE leap in the right direction, the game still needs a ton of work. I feel its better to leave a thumbs down to help encourage the devs to keep improving the game and its flaws, and give it a thumbs up when they have done this.
So, about #2. I will quote my original beefs with the PvE Tower Defense aspects of the game, and list where they currently stand now:
Here is one complaint from my original review that I feel hasnt much improved at all. Sure, they seem to have tweaked all heroes, making them a bit more "fast paced" for the PvE game mode. You seem to be able to use your abilities more often which is nice, but my main gripes about the heroes still exists:
1. Heroes are way more limited in OMDU than in past OMD games. You are stuck with 1 weapon, and have 2 abilities. There is ZERO customization when it comes to each heroes weapon and powers. No ability to equip things like amulets which grant new powers, or a different weapon for a different style of attacking.
2. Perks gained from leveling up during a match are just plain awful, boring, and most of the time something I dont even care about. Imagine someone saying, "You get to pick between these 3 different ice cream flavors" only... you dont like ice cream AND its feezing outside. So you spend a few moments trying to find the best of the worst to pick from, and go with that. Most of these "upgrade" perks are super boring. They are just too minor of a change to have any real impact on the gameplay, or any impact on how that character plays.
Most of the time I find myself asking, "Why would anyone even WANT an upgrade like that? Its pointless" or "Wow, that ugprade is so insignificantly small, its not worth taking."
The devs need to take a page from blizzards book from Heroes of the Storm (since thats a similar model to what heroes in this game follow), and look at how heroes in that game improve when they get upgrades.  A good tip: Dont do upgrades that just buff powers by a % amount. Instead, buff powers by changing how that power actually works or adding a new mechanic to that power.
Example: If a hero gets a single target stun, offer an upgrade that turns that single target stun, into an AOE slow instead as one of the options.
3. Hero Balance - This wasnt part of my original issue, but it is an issue none the less. Some heroes just feel a lot more gimpy than others. You can see these when a good player still cant get scores anywhere near what other players get with other heroes at the end of a map. This is often due to lack of AoE attacks.
Other times, like with Cyngus, its due to a dumb mechanic. In his case, its making his default hero attack the only one in the game that costs mana. There is nothing special about his attack. It makes zero sense that he must use mana just to use his default attack when no one else does.
Out of all my issues still with the game, Heroes are the one thing I feel devs still need to do LOTS of work on. Especially when it comes to level up perks, and balance between heroes. (skins need a lot of work too - THIS IS HOW YOU WILL MAKE MONEY DEVS!)
This has improved by about 50%. Its mainly a map issue. Along with update 1.6, the devs have released a handful of new maps. All of these maps are great. They allow for much better trap placement and strategy (just like orcs must die 1 and 2). No complaints here at all.
On the other hand, the original OMDunchained maps are still part of the rotation. This maps are just awful. More centered around moba "lane" gameplay. Getting one of these maps on a random game queue always makes me just want to quit out. THEY ARE NO FUN, and should be removed from the game, or completely redesigned following the examples of the newly added PvE maps. Until something like this happens, the original issue I had above is not something I feel is resolved yet.
This has been improved in almost all aspects. Due to not needing to balance traps and progress around competitive play, the assortment of traps and how you unlock them has been greatly improved upon. Compared to the first 2 games, the rate at which you unlock them, and more so, the rate at which you upgrade them, is much slower. This is to be expected with a Free 2 Play game however.
You also dont need to spend game currency on acquiring new traps (only upgrading them). This helps offset the fact that heroes also cost game currency. You instead unlock them via leveling or random reward boxes.
Overall, my original issue concerning traps has been much improved and done away with. Kudos to the dev team here.

I just bought the game, mind you - I'll edit in time if I feel something has changed about my opinion. So, my first experience with NS2 is as follows.
I hop into a server as a scrub marine. The commander is a calm as the ocean dude. I'm running around chasing some space dogs, trying all the weapons, jetpacks, etc. 40+ minutes later, Comm decides to coordinate an attack on the alien hive. As we all blast inside and I get myself an Exosuit -with railguns, because I think I'm hot ****- and mayhem ensues, Comm serenades as with 'Strangers in the Night', voice down pat. We win the raid. 10/10 would get commanded by Frank Sinatra again.
On a serious note, other than the price tag (for personal reasons, not that it was THAT expensive) I was hesitant of buying the game because I found the repeated sentiment about how the community was toxic, deterring - playing CSGO does that to you. I was still lowkey interested and often checked on the game, until the sales kicked in and we grabbed a 4-Pack as a squad. I by no means have the time nor experience to judge so far, but before I move on to more technical territory, I'd like to address the issue about the community. As you might know, both forces -Aliens and Marines- have a Commander assigned to them. The Commander has access to a top-level overview of the map, and can assign build orders for various structures, offer immediate assistance to ground forces and most importantly, coordinate attacks. Now think back to your typical competitive multiplayer FPS, : often times, simply trying to coordinate a rush between 5 people with a rifle, a pistol and a couple of grenades can get frustrating. The Commander in NS2 has to: issue build orders, heal players, provide assistance, keep tabs on enemy activity, coordinate forces, teach rookies and many more. So yes, there is some elitism both among Commanders and experienced troops, but it will rarely result in insults and flaming and overall toxicity. On the contrary, I find that it instills a certain level of realism and roleplay in the game - real-life commanders rarely sweet talk troops. So, just be friendly, humble, and listen to what the more experienced players say.

Updating this review for 1.6. Thankfully, they abandoned that MOBA garbage. They really wanted to cash in on the fact that every new-school scrub gamer likes MOBAs, but OMD is a tower defense game, and that crap has no place here. So, at the very least, they are getting their priorities in order, but there is still a ways to go before I switch this to a positive review.
First of all, my last review mentioned that the traps were lackluster and the heroes were the main method of killing enemies. That seems to have been corrected. The maps screwing up your ability to place traps in elaborate configurations is also mostly corrected.
They also have made many changes to how you earn/unlock traps and upgrades. Just before 1.6, they actually had it done (mostly) correctly, where you would earn "currency" basically, then spend that to buy/upgrade the traps you want. There were multiple types of currency, making it more convoluted than it needed to be, but at least you were getting something you can use every time you earned a reward. But in 1.6, they went back to a garbage system where it's completely random whether you get something useful or not. OMD2 had skulls and skulls alone as the currency to unlock literally everything, and that's the best possible system.
The main thing I find annoying about the game is the power creep. There was absolutely no reason for them to implement power creep in this game. For those who don't know what I mean, picture this: You are playing a map, and it's a challenge. You feel like you need to learn more and become a better player to beat it (or 5-star it). Maybe you'll play some other maps to unlock more advanced traps to use, maybe you'll recruit your friend to co-op it with you, or maybe you'll just learn a new kill-box strategy that gets the job done.
Well, with power creep, you don't need to learn♥♥♥♥♥♥ You just need to grind more levels, and your character will deal so much more damage that you just annihilate that same map that used to be a challenge. The sad thing is if they completely removed all the power creep from the enemies and players, the game wouldn't be that much different. The only two differences would be: (1) Low-level maps still require effort even when you're high level. This would allow you to actually play with your level 1 friends who just installed the game when you are level 40, rather than have them sit there while you effortlessly solo everything over and over again until they are high enough level to play the maps that challenge you. (2) High-level maps are beatable by low-level players with enough strategy and skill. As it is now, you can try endless mode starting at level 8, but you have no hope of beating even the first wave, because you do so little damage to the enemies that even the tiny fast kobolds take like 12 hits to kill. Why even bother having it unlock at that level?
Anyway, the game (OMD and OMD2) had an increasing difficulty curve already without power creep, because the more advanced monsters forced you to use new strategies. There was no need to add power creep on top of that. Literally all they accomplished with that is the removal of the two gameplay elements I listed above.
TLDR; random rewards and power creep make the game way more grindy than it should be, and I won't recommend it until both of those things are corrected.

The grind is strong with this one. Getting far in this game will require luck and a lot of grinding to find different trap cards and upgrade them. This aspect could be heavily improved. There are a ton of traps, but good luck getting them all.
I also have concerns about the longevity of the title related to the grind. You have to clear each map on each difficulty one time per hero to get chests. These chests provide you a chance to get the trap cards you need to unlock and upgrade new traps. Will you get 100% of them after clearing all of the content with all of the heroes? Am I going to be forced to buy chests for in game currency? Only time will tell, but it is a major concern.

I have actually played this game more than 35 hours. I have played a lot on the original client. I am not battle level 22 and I spent a lot of time working on my loadouts. I tried a lot to like this game because it got a huge potential which is unfortunately ruined by poor management.
Poor Description of The Game Elements
First, you feel as if the english of the developers is their second language. The heroes and the traps are poorly described. I always find myself heading to the global chat so frequently to ask other players about crucial details about traps and heroes that are either unexplained or poorly explained. Cleary, Robot need to put themselves in the players' shoes when creating these texts.
You Can't Choose Which Map to Play With Others
Second, there are almost 50 maps in this game. Each map has a different structure and different kinds of minions. That's good. Well guess what? when you want to play a match with other players, you can't choose which map you want to play. Chances are high that you will play a map you're completely bored of.
In subotage, the only game mode that is fun to play in this game imo, you can't choose which map to play. If you are thrown into a map that is completely new to you, you are screwed because it is impossible to construct your traps right from the first game with the given map. And if you are lucky to be matched with players who are experienced with this map, you're gonna feel useless either way.
Poor Matchmaking System
Robot say that they have a match making system for Subotage, it doesn't matter if this is true or not because the matching system is a joke. You will often find your self facing people with much stronger consumables, better map understanding, better gameplay, etc...

And on top of that this game adds what I'm pretty sure are the two best innovations in adventure game technology since Lucas Arts invented not killing the protagonist every five minutes:

... Just has a few outstanding issues. Not enough to not make it the best adventure game I've played in years, but enough that new players should at least be warned.

This is a fun pick-up-and-play Bomberman style of game with a focus on controls and multiplayer.  It detected my Xbox One controller without any fiddling with the settings.  I recommend it for folks looking for a fun game to play for 30-60 minutes at a time at parties, or for folks who want to enjoy a low-key competitive game for funsies.  Each full match takes maybe like 10 minutes, depending on settings and player count.
The gameplay is good.  It's standard for this genre, with good base movement speed, clear use of tiles, and nice motion tweaks that keep players from getting stuck on corners.
Multiplayer: Local and online are both supported - And lots of players can jump in at a time.  Like, up to 32 total players per match.  The leader can customize the matches with various game modes, including the standard deathmatch, as well as a "king of the hill" style match where a player tries to keep a power-up for the longest period of time, while the others try to blast them and steal it.
Quick Play: I easily got into a game without any fuss.  The online play community is relatively small at the moment, but bots are available to fill in when there aren't any other players around.  The bots themselves are pretty capable, and beat me more often than not (though I'm no expert at this game, by any means).
The controls are responsive and intuitive, and the character selection / lobby screen lets players get used to them briefly in an interesting "Walk your character through customization steps" approach.  The customization itself isn't too expansive, just lets you select one of several base characters (6 at the time of this writing), then determine primary and secondary color schemes.
The UI is utilitarian, but clear.
There's a map editor too, but I haven't checked it out in too much detail.  I was able to make a basic map and save it easy peasy, though, and I'm sure the more creative types will have fun with it.
I strongly recommend this game, again particularly for those who want some fun, quick competitive multiplayer to play with friends.  The price tag is reasonable for the amount of fun the game can give.

: Dashing Strike
: Dashing Strike
==========
Until earlier this month with the Switch release of Super Bomberman R, we had not seen hide nor hair of the old classic character. Heck, the last Bomberman title I played was on the N64. The developer of Splody sought to bring this style of gameplay back for family and friends who enjoy it. For those who do not own a Nintendo Switch or do not plan to get one, Splody is a perfectly good alternative for some fun multiplayer bombing action.
==========
In Splody, your goal is to be the last man standing. To accomplish this seemingly impossible goal, you need to gather powerups from destroyed objects and use your endless supply of bombs to blow up the opposition. The player and either bots or other players are dropped onto a random map filled with objects to blow up and obtain powerups from, along with other random obstacles. Powerups range from Bomb Ups, which increase the number of bombs you can place at once, to a DINOSAUR THAT YOU CAN RIDE. This dinosaur is actually more useful than you think, as it can take a hit for you should you fall into the line of fire.
Online multiplayer was pretty stable from what I played. If no other players are available, the game will fill in bots for you to play against until other players join in. I actually got the opportunity to play with the dev for awhile (jimbly), as you'll see in the gameplay video further down!
==========
Splody is super simple in this area. It's not great by any means but it's good enough to just jump in, not worry about it, and just have a good time. You can clearly tell what the powerups are, what/where each obstacle is, and where every bomb is placed. There should be no confusion as to anything on screen. Except maybe when you see the dinosaur mount for the first time and think to yourself "WTF?!". You can even customize your avatar with up to 6 different styles and even more colors.
==========
The few music tracks I actually noticed were pretty good. Nothing too distracting, but nothing overly ambitious either. Perhaps there's some room for improvement? Maybe...maybe even an option to load up your own music? Sound effects were pretty decent. Explosions were alright, and the little effects when picking up powerups were nice and actually matched what you were picking up.
==========
You can probably play Splody on most any modern PC. Maybe even a toaster, with 60FPS and no lag or stuttering. All of my playtime was with my Logitech F310 controller, and it was pretty much perfect. There are plenty of display, audio, and control options to play around with to meet your needs.
==========
Want a fun multiplayer party game to play with your friends? Don't want to pull out your retro consoles to play Bomberman? Don't want to shell out $300+ for a Nintendo Switch and another $50-$60 for Super Bomberman R? Pick up Splody!

Ok, I need to preface this by stating the following:
1.) I was born in the early '80s.
2.) My parents were Yankees.
3.) I'm whiter than cottage cheese.
To that end I have no real idea if the racism in this game is accurate or a caricature, honestly. I suspect it's somewhere in the middle.
I both enjoyed and was frustrated by this game. It's not really a clear thumbs-up thumbs-down vote. A lot of people will get a lot of enjoyment out of it. There's a lot to do, a lot to see, and a lot to collect. However, those of us, myself included, who want a fleshed out story will be a bit lacking. The game does a lot well, but it has some glaring problems that are, frankly, unforgivable.
Here's the positives first:
1.) The soundtrack is killer. I got the game at a deep discount and the soundtrack alone is well worth what I paid for. It has a great combination of '60s rock, R&B, and pop hits (amongst others). It's a lot of fun to outrun police to the tune of "Palisades Park" by Freddy Cannon or have a shootout in a quarry to the tune of "Folsom Prison Blues" by Johnny Cash. The developers knew how to use music effectively and did it very well.
2.) The map is quite large. This is somewhat a positive AND a negative as it takes a while to get anywhere. However, the "GPS" system works quite well and it's very easy to get around with the help of the minimap. This leads to...
3.) The UI is (generally) well designed. When driving you have a rear view mirror and can easily spin the camera around to see what's going on behind you. The speedometer and tacometer are unobtrusive, if a bit useless. The minimap is great. While on foot, it's easy to see how much ammo you are carrying and your health/armor levels. I also never had any signifigant issues with using something I didn't intend to. The game makes it very clear what item it is you are going to do an action to. There are minor issues when two objects are placed too close to each other, but those are typically insignificant. The game also utilizes several different hotkeys to do different things, so you are never in any real danger of picking up a dead body instead of a dropped weapon.
4.) The vehicles generally behaved realistically. As someone who has driven several vehicles from the mid to late 1960s, I can confirm that they are generally just as sluggish and heavy as they are in the game. In fact, I would say the vehicles in the game perform better than their real-life counterparts.
5.) I personally enjoyed the way the game handled the full cutscenes. The jumps in time were handled well and I really liked watching them. They told the story from a Discovery channel esque "real crime" drama taking place in the 2010s. It was unique and I liked the idea.
Now we get to the cons. Some of these are excusable and could potentially have been fixed by patches. Some are inherent flaws in the game that cannot be fixed.
1.) The graphics are generally poor and unoptimized. I tend to ignore graphics so long as they don't royally suck. These are not great. You can tell this is a poorly done console port. This could potentially be excused if the gameplay was good, but that leads us to...
2.) The gameplay (after the first act) is dull and repetitious. The first act is done well. It hops around in time (like the cutscenes) and is scriped well. It's generally fun. Afterward, though, is a repetitious wreck. Basically, you shoot badguys and cause general havok in a specific area until the miniboss shows up. You kill him, do the shooting and havoking a second time until the second miniboss shows up. Kill him too. Then the district boss shows up. The boss levels are usually reasonably entertaining and it's clear THIS was where the real polish was done. Unfortunately you have to do this NINE TIMES. It's dull after the first few and the game doesn't really give you any good reason to want to do it again as all the districts are basically the same bunch of minigames with different settings. Even THIS would be excusable (somewhat) if the following wasn't true:
3.) The AI sucks chocolate salty balls. Don't get me wrong, it's not the worst I've ever seen, but that's usually reserved for games that are broken. The AI does exactly what it's supposed to. Unfortunately, the AI is very very stupid. Case in point: run up to enemy location, hide around the wall from a bad guy, and whistle. It doesn't matter if you are on a construction site with a lot of civilian AI that's noisy as hell or a shack in the middle of the bayou; ONE SINGLE enemy will investigate. If you have two talking only ONE will investigate. If you run up to a group of five only ONE will investigate. They will ALWAYS investigate. Again, it doesn't matter where you are or if a whistle could conceivibly be a commonly heard sound. The AI will ALWAYS wander toward the sound like a sorority girl investigating a dark basement. They stroll toward you and practically BEG you to kill them. Rinse and repeat until someone finally sees you long enough for some arbitrary flag to fire and you are in unending combat.
4.) The police exist to do nothing but kill the PC. This is an extention of the prior but it needs an entry on its own. The police do not fight crime in New Bordeaux. They do not protect the innocent. They exist ONLY to kill a SINGLE PERSON: Lincoln Clay. If you get into a shootout with ANYONE and they respond, they will zero in on the PC like a AMRAAM. It doesn't matter who you're fighting or how many civilians are getting killed by the enemy's molotovs: if YOU are fighting they will try to kill YOU. There's also no system of justice either: shoot a civilian, get shot; shoot a car, get shot; shoot a mobster, get shot; break into a store, get shot; break into a telephone exchange, get shot; run over a pedestrian, get shot; lighly rearend a police car, get shot; walk too close to a cop, get shot. On the other hand, burning through a red light at 115 MPH, they don't bat an eye. Mafia I, which was released in 2002, had a VASTLY more sophisticated system of law and order. Let me repeat that: Mafia I, which is currently a FIFTEEN-YEAR-OLD game, actually had a system where you had to follow the traffic laws and the cops wouldn't gun you down for a fender-bender. They also suffer from the "GTA V effect" and materialize from juuuust out of view and swarm you.
5.) After you finish off a ward, there's not really anything to do there. I can't fault Mafia III exclusively as this is generally a problem with open world games in general, but once you take over a ward there's not much point in ever setting foot there. It's interesting to see the businesses change when they change hands, but once you collect all the Playboys and Vargas drawings, there's not much reason to go back. This leads us to...
6.) The collectables are a tad-bit silly and really really pointless. I like vintage playboys and Vargas illustrations as much as the next man. However, this is because I am, in fact, a man. Enough said. However, this illustrates a further issue:
7.) There's not any particular "advancement" in the game. As far as I can tell, you are given all the clothing at the beginning of the game. This was rather disappointing to me as I hoped to unlock additional cosmetic features as I went along. This was not the case so I switched between looking like Laurence Fishburne in "Apocalypse Now" to Laurence Fishburne playing Malcom X to an extra from "Shaft." In addition, you have a large variety of weapons, that are pretty much ALL available at the beginning of the game, and are all pretty dull. The Colt 1911 was pretty much the same as the Browning 9mm which was pretty much the same as the Colt Python.
In conclusion (since I'm running low on space) the game is not really worth it IMO unless you enjoy doing the same thing over and over to really good music.

A really fun and short little game (disregard the 220+ hours, most of that is from the game being left on in the background over several days.) in the match three style of gameplay. Essentially the top fourth of the screne is used for showing monsters, chests, and doors. The bottome three fourths of the screne is where all of the tile matching takes place. There are 6 tile types. There is the sword tile, which does the most damage and has the highest chance to crit. The staff/wand icon which is a ranged attack and has a percent chance to inflict some kind of status aliment. There is the armor icon which allows you to take more hits before your run ends. The chest icon can give you useful 1 use items that do damage, or swaps tiles for others. The key icon is pretty obvious...it unlocks things, chests take two keys (can be changed through an upgrading system) and one key for doors. Finally there are the resourse icons (stone and wood). You can use the resourses to give yourself premanent buffs, like making chests open in one key. There is also a quest system per "floor" of the dungeon. The quests yield rewards like gold, which is used to upgrade your sword, armor, and staff icons, among other things. Quests also provide you with purple essense which is the currency fro the permanent buffs.
All in all there is actully quite a nice little bit of depth, and for the price it is well worth it. I would say the average completion time is maybe 8-12 hours depending on hour good you are at match 3s.

To start: Gameforge, the people managing this game in the EU have opted to not give EU customers free coins for logging in where the US customers do get a small amount of premium currency with some regularity for logging in.
Review: As of the time of this review, this game feels like a poor mans Orcs Must Die and is fairly exploitative in the way it makes its players grind for upgrades in order to progress which can ofcourse be bought with premium currency in random loot crates. The game also features premium only skins on top of the premium loot boxes needed to progress.
Traps feel fairly weak in this game when not upgraded, meaning that the emphasis is more on grinding out those flat percentage upgrades for your traps over strategy and with the huge amount of potential loot in the game your chances of getting the item you need is considerably lower, only further reinforcing the need to obtain more and more boxes.
Oh and if that wasn't bad enough, the amount of boxes you can earn is finite with 2 being available per level completion and 1 sub-par box per completion with each character and one that can be obtained daily through a challenge.
Weapons are weak, static (Not changeable) and do not score headshots.
The matchmaking is also pretty terrible with no pre or post-game lobby, often poor connections and no guarantee that your teammates have the upgrades required for the level in question.
I would love to give it a higher rating as I love the orcs must die series but I cannot in good conscience even slightly recommend a game that predates on the wallets of people who are vulnerable to gambling addiction.
I would only recommend this to people who are going to play this game totally for free; very casually or with a set group of friends.

Ok, I need to preface this by stating the following:
1.) I was born in the early '80s.
2.) My parents were Yankees.
3.) I'm whiter than cottage cheese.
To that end I have no real idea if the racism in this game is accurate or a caricature, honestly. I suspect it's somewhere in the middle.
I both enjoyed and was frustrated by this game. It's not really a clear thumbs-up thumbs-down vote. A lot of people will get a lot of enjoyment out of it. There's a lot to do, a lot to see, and a lot to collect. However, those of us, myself included, who want a fleshed out story will be a bit lacking. The game does a lot well, but it has some glaring problems that are, frankly, unforgivable.
Here's the positives first:
1.) The soundtrack is killer. I got the game at a deep discount and the soundtrack alone is well worth what I paid for. It has a great combination of '60s rock, R&B, and pop hits (amongst others). It's a lot of fun to outrun police to the tune of "Palisades Park" by Freddy Cannon or have a shootout in a quarry to the tune of "Folsom Prison Blues" by Johnny Cash. The developers knew how to use music effectively and did it very well.
2.) The map is quite large. This is somewhat a positive AND a negative as it takes a while to get anywhere. However, the "GPS" system works quite well and it's very easy to get around with the help of the minimap. This leads to...
3.) The UI is (generally) well designed. When driving you have a rear view mirror and can easily spin the camera around to see what's going on behind you. The speedometer and tacometer are unobtrusive, if a bit useless. The minimap is great. While on foot, it's easy to see how much ammo you are carrying and your health/armor levels. I also never had any signifigant issues with using something I didn't intend to. The game makes it very clear what item it is you are going to do an action to. There are minor issues when two objects are placed too close to each other, but those are typically insignificant. The game also utilizes several different hotkeys to do different things, so you are never in any real danger of picking up a dead body instead of a dropped weapon.
4.) The vehicles generally behaved realistically. As someone who has driven several vehicles from the mid to late 1960s, I can confirm that they are generally just as sluggish and heavy as they are in the game. In fact, I would say the vehicles in the game perform better than their real-life counterparts.
5.) I personally enjoyed the way the game handled the full cutscenes. The jumps in time were handled well and I really liked watching them. They told the story from a Discovery channel esque "real crime" drama taking place in the 2010s. It was unique and I liked the idea.
Now we get to the cons. Some of these are excusable and could potentially have been fixed by patches. Some are inherent flaws in the game that cannot be fixed.
1.) The graphics are generally poor and unoptimized. I tend to ignore graphics so long as they don't royally suck. These are not great. You can tell this is a poorly done console port. This could potentially be excused if the gameplay was good, but that leads us to...
2.) The gameplay (after the first act) is dull and repetitious. The first act is done well. It hops around in time (like the cutscenes) and is scriped well. It's generally fun. Afterward, though, is a repetitious wreck. Basically, you shoot badguys and cause general havok in a specific area until the miniboss shows up. You kill him, do the shooting and havoking a second time until the second miniboss shows up. Kill him too. Then the district boss shows up. The boss levels are usually reasonably entertaining and it's clear THIS was where the real polish was done. Unfortunately you have to do this NINE TIMES. It's dull after the first few and the game doesn't really give you any good reason to want to do it again as all the districts are basically the same bunch of minigames with different settings. Even THIS would be excusable (somewhat) if the following wasn't true:
3.) The AI sucks chocolate salty balls. Don't get me wrong, it's not the worst I've ever seen, but that's usually reserved for games that are broken. The AI does exactly what it's supposed to. Unfortunately, the AI is very very stupid. Case in point: run up to enemy location, hide around the wall from a bad guy, and whistle. It doesn't matter if you are on a construction site with a lot of civilian AI that's noisy as hell or a shack in the middle of the bayou; ONE SINGLE enemy will investigate. If you have two talking only ONE will investigate. If you run up to a group of five only ONE will investigate. They will ALWAYS investigate. Again, it doesn't matter where you are or if a whistle could conceivibly be a commonly heard sound. The AI will ALWAYS wander toward the sound like a sorority girl investigating a dark basement. They stroll toward you and practically BEG you to kill them. Rinse and repeat until someone finally sees you long enough for some arbitrary flag to fire and you are in unending combat.
4.) The police exist to do nothing but kill the PC. This is an extention of the prior but it needs an entry on its own. The police do not fight crime in New Bordeaux. They do not protect the innocent. They exist ONLY to kill a SINGLE PERSON: Lincoln Clay. If you get into a shootout with ANYONE and they respond, they will zero in on the PC like a AMRAAM. It doesn't matter who you're fighting or how many civilians are getting killed by the enemy's molotovs: if YOU are fighting they will try to kill YOU. There's also no system of justice either: shoot a civilian, get shot; shoot a car, get shot; shoot a mobster, get shot; break into a store, get shot; break into a telephone exchange, get shot; run over a pedestrian, get shot; lighly rearend a police car, get shot; walk too close to a cop, get shot. On the other hand, burning through a red light at 115 MPH, they don't bat an eye. Mafia I, which was released in 2002, had a VASTLY more sophisticated system of law and order. Let me repeat that: Mafia I, which is currently a FIFTEEN-YEAR-OLD game, actually had a system where you had to follow the traffic laws and the cops wouldn't gun you down for a fender-bender. They also suffer from the "GTA V effect" and materialize from juuuust out of view and swarm you.
5.) After you finish off a ward, there's not really anything to do there. I can't fault Mafia III exclusively as this is generally a problem with open world games in general, but once you take over a ward there's not much point in ever setting foot there. It's interesting to see the businesses change when they change hands, but once you collect all the Playboys and Vargas drawings, there's not much reason to go back. This leads us to...
6.) The collectables are a tad-bit silly and really really pointless. I like vintage playboys and Vargas illustrations as much as the next man. However, this is because I am, in fact, a man. Enough said. However, this illustrates a further issue:
7.) There's not any particular "advancement" in the game. As far as I can tell, you are given all the clothing at the beginning of the game. This was rather disappointing to me as I hoped to unlock additional cosmetic features as I went along. This was not the case so I switched between looking like Laurence Fishburne in "Apocalypse Now" to Laurence Fishburne playing Malcom X to an extra from "Shaft." In addition, you have a large variety of weapons, that are pretty much ALL available at the beginning of the game, and are all pretty dull. The Colt 1911 was pretty much the same as the Browning 9mm which was pretty much the same as the Colt Python.
In conclusion (since I'm running low on space) the game is not really worth it IMO unless you enjoy doing the same thing over and over to really good music.

Story and characters - I was very skeptical about buying this game. With a 48% (at the time of writing) positive rating on steam, of coarse there was going to be some skepticism. I played the demo and the day after I played it, I went and bought it. I gotta say that it's a very fun game! A lot of people give this game flack for having repetative missions but honestly I didn't find them repetative. I know that they ARE repetative as the missions are as followed: kill some bad guys to draw out mini bosses, then kill mini bosses to draw out the big boss then move to a new area and rinse and repeat. After doing this about seven times (can't remember how many bosses there are) you get to the big boss. The final enemy. So the missions are repetative but they just didnt feel like a grind. They felt really fun. The story is well paced and shot as an action/crime drama with very nice cutscenes with fenominal lip syncronization. The story is very nicely paced and FILLED with interesting characters, places, and items to find throughout the world. Anywhere from the 60s Playboy magazines (those are always fun ;D) to the Hotrod magazines the collectables are interesting and hystorically accurate. The games characters- they all seem to have a unique relationship with Lincoln and as you play you get to delve into their past. Some examples from this are finding out what happened to Joe in Mafia 2 and regaining the trust of Hatian mob leader Cassandra. All in all the story is very fun and the characters are interesting, well paced and fleshed out. The main character especially (Lincoln Clay) isn't portrayed as some innocent man whos had wrong done to him. He was apart of the black mob before he left for Vietnam and after he returned. Lincoln is a killer who isn't afraid to put his victims up on display for the public to see and is willing to kill anyone in his way by use of brutal and grotesque killings. Lincoln is clearly a man who has gone over the edge and is almost as evil as the people hes going after, but yet, the game makes you feel sympathetic for him.
Game World - The game world also feels very alive with the hystorically accurate racism that your character faces. When you commit a crime in the Hollow (the ghetto/black neighborhood) and have the cops called on you, the dispatcher will often say something such as "there is an armed negro male in the Hollow if your in the area and wan't to check it out" where as if you commit the same crim in a white neighborhood the dispatcher will order her officers to get there ASAP.  When you enter some shops and resturants you are asked to leave because "colored folk aren't aloud" and eventually you will have the police phoned on you. The police/phone mechanic. I love this mechanic! It is so cool that when civilians witness a crime the police don't just all of a sudden go after you as if they have hidden cameras watching your every move. In other open world games such as GTA V (fantastic game btw) when you commit a crime you are automatically wanted whereas in Mafia 3 the civillians have to run to the nearest payphone and call the police meaning that if you take the civillian out the cops won't show up. Overall, hystorically accurate and lively.
Graphics and Optimization - Graphics in this game look pretty good. They aren't drop dead gorgeous and seem to have a grainy and gray look to them sometimes. While the textures aren't the sharpest, the phenomional lighting effects and other effects (such as raindrops) look very appealing to the eye. Draw distance is a little lackluster but it's not a deal breaker. As for how the game runs, its okay at best. I have a GTX 1060 6GB and an i5-6500 so it's not the most powerful but nothing to scoff at, yet the game doesnt run at a consistant 60 fps at medium settings. In combat and when running the game maintains 60 at medium, however once you get into a car and start to floor it the game dips to high 40s. However, the difference between low and high graphics settings is miniscule and hardly noticable and even on lowest preset with everything low as it can go or off, the game still looks better than it's console counterpart with longer draw distances and higher res shadows.
Music and Sound - Oh my GOD!!! The Music in this game is ♥♥♥♥ing excellent, from the lower toned blues hits of the time to the twangy country music to the stellar rock and roll guitar licks heard in classic 60s rock, the music is phenominal and with over 100 songs I find myself still finding new songs on teh radio that I had no idea were included (All Along the Watchertower by Jimi Hendrix, Born on the Bayou by CCR). While not everyone will enjoy the music, those who do find that era of music interesting will love the soundtrack. In one of the early missions you have to escape the police by way of boat in an underground sewer and as soon as it plops you into the boat Born to Be Wild starts blasting and you just feel so badass. As for sound, the sound is excellent as well all the way from the old 60s horns on vehicles, the whiny police sirens to the low end base sound of a shotgun blast the sound is always satisfying and does an excellent job to keep you immersed. The thumping of your boat as you hit the trough between waves has a nice satisfying sound to it and the car engines have a nice low end rumble to them. Enemies also have little side chats to eachother which is well recorded and the main characters voice in cutscenes makes you feel like you're really there. All in all very good sound design and great song choices.
Mechanics - While the driving personally took some time to get into, it's not bad by any stretch of the imagination. Mafia 3 has a sticky and arcady feel to the vehicles where you never seem to spin out Once you get used to the sticky feel of the vehicles though, drifting your way into gunfights and then jumping out of your still moving vehicle is a blast. Combat is excellent with a descent variety of weapons to choose from that all feel a little bit unique in their own way. The enemy AI is more realistic compared to other games. Some good examples are that while a barrage of bullets is being blasted at you from one direction the enemy will send someone to flank you from either side. I consider myself to be a pretty good 3rd person shooter player and can do quite well in those types of games but even I found myself getting flanked and in some cases killed on medium difficulty. Another example of the AI that Is unique is if you move from your cover to another piece of cover without the enemy seeing you, they will shoot at your last location instead of where you are. One final thing that is unique to the game's combat is the stealth. What kind of open world game would this be without stealth am I right? Well this game believe it or not has better stealth mechanics than Assassin's Creed (a stealth-based game). In both games you can whistle from behind cover and attract one enemy, hower ever in Assassin's creed you can continuously call over enemies and none of them will realize that their friend has just gone missing whereas in Mafia 3 if you call over an enemy he will look for you and you can kill him, but if you call over a seccond enemy, they will equip their weapon and act a lot more keen and objective, then if you whistle over a third enemy, they will open fire on your assumed position. Overall the game feels smooth and fun to play.
SHORTENED VERSION - Pros: Good looking game, a lot of fun to play, interesting characters and world, fantastic sound design, good AI, unique time period. Negatives: Some will find the game repetative, optimization is meh, strange driving mechanics (somewhere between Watch Dogs and GTA V). Overall a fun game that I would reccomend. However I would reccomend getting this game on sale or on a game key website instead of buying at full price.

When it comes to best multiplayer arcade-like games, Duck Game is of the first I think of.
It runs well, and framerate issues are minimal and non-intrusive under standard play. It also supports the easy-to-use, reliable Steam interface for online multiplayer.
On the standandpoint of content, there is plenty of fun things to do with your friends, or alone. However, I do admit that this game is only a fraction as entertaining when it is played alone, and should therefore be considered to be essentially, a multiplayer-only game. The base game has plenty of interesting weapons, levels and customization, that integrates well with the enjoyment of playing with friends. However, after a while, one can learn all the default content, and enjoyment can begin to stagnate. This is where the Steam workshop comes in handy, allowing a plethora of changes and additions to be added to the game, allowing the experience to stay fresh.
Finally, the game fits perfectly into a context of a medium to large friend gathering. As long as everyone has a controller or other input device, games can quickly be cycled, with no player staying out for long periods of time. This game definitely posses the "just one more turn" drive, and time can dissapear before you know it while playing. It's play style also means that the game heavily emphasizes skill, and victory relies far less on pure chance. All these factors combined, render this a fantastic choice to play at your next friend gathering. Just don't forget your gamepad.

Brief Summary:
I would definitely recommend this to those who like the old Monkey Island games. Probably one of the best purchases I've made on steam, although that may just have had something to do with getting it on a sale.
Got some outstanding bugs though, so if you do buy it: Save frequently, and don't worry if the characters sometimes behave a bit... Well, like disguised humanoid robots encountering a glitch.
More in-depth:
If you've played the Monkey Island games you know what to expect. If you haven't, here's what: Wacky humor, mostly somewhat logical puzzles... Usually. A goofy protagonist whose actions frequently have unexpected and hilarious consequences, and a thrilling and engaging story. And a love interest, of course. The hero can't get the girl if there isn't a girl to get.
And on top of that this game adds what I'm pretty sure are the two best innovations in adventure game technology since Lucas Arts invented not killing the protagonist every five minutes:
All in all, so far it's the best adventure game I've played in some years.
... Just has a few outstanding issues. Not enough to not make it the best adventure game I've played in years, but enough that new players should at least be warned.
The issues are mostly bugs, but there are some other problems.
But other than that it's mostly just bugs. They aren't super bad or anything, but they are rather obvious, and raises the question of whether anybody even played the game through from start to finish before release.

The Witcher 2 is sequel to The Witcher (which is actually a really boring game in which developpers took too many risks that didn't really pay off ; and I wouldn't recommend you to buy it). You are Geralt of Rivia, a Witcher (some kind of Mutant with magical powers and high sword mastery) and you have friends (!!) that follow you in your quest, aka regain your memory.
What is a Witcher :
At the end of The Witcher, Geralt saves King Foltest from another witcher's assassination attemp and afterwards Foltest asks him to join and protect him. At the beginning of The Witcher 2, Foltest does die and Geralt is somehow accused by the entire realm. His quest will then be to find the real assassin and to burnish his acts. So despite his notorious "neutrality" the famed witcher Geralt will be forced to make alliances and choices that will define his story and most importantly the story of the world around him.
And this is what I enjoyed the most in The Witcher 2 : its non-linearity that makes it highly replayable. I'm not spoiling anything but in chapter 1 you are given the opportunity to make a choice that will COMPLETELY CHANGE THE GAME (I'm talking WHOLE DIFFERENTS AREAS AND QUESTS !) ; so when you buy this game it's like you're buying not just one but 2 or 3 games, son ! And the quests are really attracting in the sense that you will really want to do that sidequest because it's fun and well designed... and you need money to stop dying in two hits with your naked butt.
Let's talk about the character and the lore : The Witcher's universe is a very dense and complex universe, hence you should feel free to have the wiki open next to you when you play the game (of course making sure you don't spoil yourself too much) to make sure that you can enjoy every bit of this complex universe and not just give up because "♥♥♥♥ it, the story is too complicated and what the ♥♥♥♥ is that amnesia people are all talking about".
Characters in the Witcher are designed so that they are all different, all have political implications and are memorable thanks to their design, agressivity, sexual orientation/relationships with the hero since The Witcher 2 is a mature game (sex boys !) ; or whatever... The graphics and level of details given throughout the entire game also helps a lot with this (yeah the game is one of the best-looking thing ever designed and I hope you upgrade your PC or it could have a bad time).
The universe in which you play in is pretty big although it is far from being any kind of open world. The developpers focused on bringing some kind of "medieval reality" back to life. Reality is something important in The Witcher and you will have to deal with both small fighting areas and huge lands.
Fighting and the combat system may give you a hard time at first (do not hesitate to change the difficulty level to easy if you're more of a casual player and difficulty prevents you from enjoying the game), but I hope that like me you will feel like it's one of the best and realistic combat systems ever designed : Geralt isn't immortal, he dies fast, however he can roll like a car tyre. If you are really having a hard time in the early stages then don't give up and let me tell you that the game becomes easier as Geralt levels up (which goes really fast with the main quest, and there is a max level of 35).
Hardcore gamers rejoice, Dark Mode is here for you. Get ready to cry if you do it on your first playthrough.
The Witcher 2 is unique and I deeply thing any kind of player can enjoy it in some way, probably the best RPG of its generation, I found the story much more compelling than Skyrim and have to go with the

Well, Dark Crusade is an expansion pack for the popular RTS series Warhammer 40k: Dawn of War. Since I was a big Warhammer fan at that time I decided to try it out. Dark Crusade introduces The Necrons and the Taus as the new races while also tweak the balancing units and changing the single player. What made Dawn of War Dark Cr unique? The races with each unique look and units and are all unique ways that may suit your style to play as, Blood and gore was glorious, the maps are beautiful and immersive fitting the 40k universe and designed perfectly I don't recall it ever being unbalanced or bad, customizing your army for mp like colors and logos, sync kills which were executions animations when you kill an enemy unit, the music was perfect and each race has their unique theme and music, the voices are top notch and badass fitting for every race. Just youtube search Eliphas the Inheritor voice lines and you'll see why they're awesome. Play the god damn Single Player and if you have friends play some MP together. It's a fun game and for some advice do not play the Necrons if you have started. I recommend playing the Orks, CSM, SM and learning the basics of the game before jumping to other races.
Also, I recommend this review of the game by Thunderpsyker he gives a really good insight into the game and explains more further into detail about the game that I cbf writing on here.
TL:DR
Get the Master Pack for Dawn of War and Dark Crusade is an great RTS expansion pack for a legendary game series and a good way to get into 40k if you never heard of it. Out of all of them play Dark Crusade is the best out of all of them imo.

I recently finished 10,000,000 and had a great time doing so. You can fire it up quickly to play a couple of rounds or you can get stuck to it for a hour, because it has the "just one more run" feel to it.
Your goal is to accumulate 10,000,000 points by repeatedly entering a dungeon, slaying monsters and grabbing loot. Your run is over once your hero is pushed out of the left side of the screen. The screen keeps moving right as long as you are standing still, frantically trying to spot fitting tiles and you are pushed further back by monster attacks.
Once you reach a door or a chest, you want to find and match key tiles to grab gold or items. If there is a monster ahead, you can match sword- or staff tiles to either trigger a physical or a magical attack (some are more vulnerable to magic, some to physical damage). If you match wood- or stone tiles, you gather resources to upgrade the rooms in your hub. They grant access to the blacksmith to upgrade your sword or the alchemist to use powerful potions and many more. This gives a great feel of progression. Your first runs might be over in about 30 seconds, but the more you grind and unlock, the longer you survive in the dungeon.
What makes this game so entertaining are the split second decisions you have to make. You might see an enemy behind a crate: to get to match 3 key tiles you would have to sacrifice 4 sword tiles, but they are necessary to fight the monster ahead. Can you find another solution that opens both the crate and gives you 3 or more tiles to attack the enemy, before the time runs out? Remember: the worst move, is no move!
If you are a fan of match 3 games and (grindy) dungeon crawlers, you should check this one out. They are combined flawlessly here.

It took me around 17 hours to 100% all the levels. That being said, it's rare that I actually try to fully complete a game... Let alone a side scroller.
I would definitely recommend this game if it goes on sale, and at the 15 dollar price I would also recommend it to some, but there are problems to it. The combat is relatively simple, and if you purposely lower your attack damage then it can get somewhat boring due to the limited moves. I've found a lot of the fun to come from progression (Finding secrets, getting better items, and leveling up). The combat isn't bad by any means: I've found it to be pretty satisfiyng. However, I didn't feel any incentive to play the game stylishly. Early on, I got a 1000 combo simply because a side quest asked me to... aside from that, I got the best items available and killed enemies as quickly as possible. I wish I didn't so so against bosses, as they were very unsatisfying (I killed them too quickly). I found the most satisfying aspect of the combat to be the parrying. My biggest concern however, is that the game doesn't have much replay value to me. What happens after you beat the game, is that you simply have the option to load back to your game saves. There's no new game plus option, and so I would highly recommend just going onto Hard mode if you buy this game.
Overall, I really enjoyed the game. There are very few side scrollers that I've completed: Final Fight 3, Turtles in TIme, Pixel Junk Shooter, Sonic 3. At least, these are the only games I can think of currently.Games such as Mega Man never interested me (mainly due to their high difficulty). On normal difficulty, this game isn't very challenging at all (and even though I enjoy easy games, I wanted more challenge to this game). Giving my character 0.1x damage makes the game feel like a patience test. I would strongly recommend playing on Hard mode. I found that this balances things nicely.
This being said, I think this is very well made. I loved the backtracking, and I constantly found myself going after the smallest collectibles.
